title: [Trainer/Modeling] Forward **kwargs to self.loss_function in generic classification heads and vision models
body:
# What does this PR do?

Fixes #47688

### Problem
`Trainer` determines whether loss needs `/ gradient_accumulation_steps` normalization by inspecting whether the model accepts loss keyword arguments (checking if `**kwargs` is present in `model.forward`). When `**kwargs` is declared, `Trainer` injects `num_items_in_batch` into `forward` and skips its own division under the expectation that `self.loss_function` / `fixed_cross_entropy` will normalize the loss by `num_items_in_batch`.

However:
1. `GenericForSequenceClassification` and `GenericForTokenClassification` in `src/transformers/modeling_layers.py` (which are inherited by almost all modern decoder models including Llama, Qwen, Mistral, Gemma, Phi, SmolLM, etc.) declared `**kwargs` in `forward` but did not pass `**kwargs` to `self.loss_function`.
2. Several vision classification models (e.g. `Swinv2ForImageClassification`, `DonutSwinForImageClassification`, `ResNetForImageClassification`, `RegNetForImageClassification`, `SiglipForImageClassification`, `Siglip2ForImageClassification`) also omitted `**kwargs` when calling `self.loss_function`.

As a result, `fixed_cross_entropy` defaulted to `reduction="mean"` without token-level scaling, while `Trainer` skipped its gradient accumulation division, causing the loss to be inflated by `gradient_accumulation_steps`.

### Solution
- Forward `**kwargs` to `self.loss_function` in `GenericForSequenceClassification` and `GenericForTokenClassification` in `src/transformers/modeling_layers.py`.
- Forward `**kwargs` to `self.loss_function` in `Swinv2ForImageClassification`, `DonutSwinForImageClassification`, `ResNetForImageClassification`, `RegNetForImageClassification`, `SiglipForImageClassification`, and `Siglip2ForImageClassification`.
- Added `test_loss_num_items_in_batch_scaling` to `ModelTesterMixin` in `tests/test_modeling_common.py` to verify that when `num_items_in_batch` is passed, the raw unscaled loss sum (`loss * num_items_in_batch`) remains invariant.

title: [Video] Fix convert_to_rgb channel slicing and alpha blending for RGBA videos
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48053)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48053)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #48051

### Problem
1. In `src/transformers/video_utils.py::convert_to_rgb`, `infer_channel_dimension_format(video)` was called without `num_channels=(1, 3, 4)`, which raised `ValueError: Unable to infer channel dimension format` for 4-channel RGBA videos.
2. In the alpha-blending formula of `video_utils.py::convert_to_rgb`, `video[..., 3, :, :]` (the 1-channel alpha tensor) was mistakenly multiplied as the foreground colors instead of `video[..., :3, :, :]` (the 3 RGB channels). This caused incorrect shapes (e.g. `(2, 2, 1, 1)` instead of `(2, 3, 1, 1)`) and corrupted pixel values.
3. In both `video_utils.py::convert_to_rgb` and `video_processing_utils.py::BaseVideoProcessor.convert_to_rgb`, fully opaque RGBA inputs returned `video` with 4 channels rather than stripping the alpha channel to return 3 RGB channels (`video[..., :3, :, :]`).

### Solution
- Updated `infer_channel_dimension_format(video, num_channels=(1, 3, 4))` in `video_utils.py::convert_to_rgb`.
- Fixed the alpha blending formula to use `video[..., :3, :, :]` as foreground.
- Return `video[..., :3, :, :]` for opaque 4-channel RGBA inputs across both numpy (`video_utils.py`) and torch (`video_processing_utils.py`) implementations.
- Added unit tests in `tests/utils/test_video_utils.py` covering transparent and opaque RGBA numpy and torch inputs.

title: Add token-level chat input sanitization
body:
Concrete version of my review on #47386: no text-level escaping, `split_special_tokens=True` is the safety boundary. Content is wrapped in `UntrustedInput` (`tokenize_securely()`, callable from Jinja), template text is encoded normally around it, so Jinja formats and the tokenizer decides what is a control token.

Same API (`sanitize_special_tokens=True`), ~250 lines instead of ~520, and a chat with nothing to sanitize encodes byte-identically. cc @Rocketknight1

Pretty sure we can even do better. We should just use the flags provided by `tokenizers`.

title: convert_to_rgb gives wrong output shape for RGBA numpy videos
body:
## System Info

- transformers main (commit 8c62d6f)
- Windows 11, Python 3.13
- numpy

## Who can help?

@molbap @guarin

## Reproduction

Was processing some RGBA video frames as numpy arrays and noticed the output shape is wrong after `convert_to_rgb`. Here's a minimal example:

```python
import numpy as np
from transformers.video_utils import convert_to_rgb

video = np.array(
    [
        [[[255, 0, 0, 128]]],
        [[[0, 255, 0, 64]]],
    ],
    dtype=np.uint8,
)

rgb_video = convert_to_rgb(video, input_data_format="channels_last")
print(rgb_video.shape)  # prints (2, 2, 1, 1) — should be (2, 3, 1, 1)
```

Looks like the blending line in `convert_to_rgb` (video_utils.py:789) uses `video[..., 3, :, :]` as the foreground instead of `video[..., :3, :, :]`, so the alpha channel ends up being used as the RGB data. This causes both the wrong channel count and incorrect pixel values.

## Expected behavior

Output shape should be `(2, 3, 1, 1)` — 3 RGB channels after blending the alpha with white background. The alpha channel should be used for blending only, not as the foreground color.

title: [Siglip] Return hidden_states and attentions in SiglipTextTransformer and SiglipVisionTransformer
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48049)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48049)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #42759

### Problem
In `SiglipTextTransformer.forward` and `SiglipVisionTransformer.forward`, `encoder_outputs` computed `hidden_states` and `attentions`, but `BaseModelOutputWithPooling` was constructed with only `last_hidden_state` and `pooler_output`. Consequently, passing `output_hidden_states=True` or `output_attentions=True` to `SiglipModel`, `SiglipTextModel`, or `SiglipVisionModel` returned `None` for `hidden_states` and `attentions` in the outputs.

### Solution
- Pass `hidden_states=encoder_outputs.hidden_states` and `attentions=encoder_outputs.attentions` when constructing `BaseModelOutputWithPooling` in `SiglipTextTransformer.forward` and `SiglipVisionTransformer.forward`.
- Add a unit test in `tests/models/siglip/test_modeling_siglip.py` validating that `outputs.text_model_output` and `outputs.vision_model_output` contain the expected layer hidden states and attention weights when `output_hidden_states=True` and `output_attentions=True`.

title: [Siglip/Siglip2] Fix default vocab_size and token_id bounds in text config
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48048)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48048)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #47612

### Problem
1. In `SiglipTextConfig`, `bos_token_id` was defaulted to `49406` and `eos_token_id` to `49407` (inherited from CLIP defaults), while `vocab_size` is `32000`. This caused `PreTrainedConfig.validate_token_ids()` to raise warnings on instantiation that `bos_token_id` (49406) and `eos_token_id` (49407) are not within vocabulary (between 0 and 31999).
2. In `Siglip2TextConfig`, `vocab_size` was defaulted to `32000` from `SiglipTextConfig` rather than `256000` (Gemma tokenizer vocab size used by SigLIP2), which similarly triggered vocabulary out-of-bounds warnings when instantiating or loading checkpoints like `google/siglip2-base-patch16-naflex`.

### Solution
- Set `bos_token_id: int | None = None` and `eos_token_id: int | list[int] | None = 1` in `SiglipTextConfig` to match SentencePiece token conventions and vocabulary bounds.
- Set `vocab_size: int = 256000` in `Siglip2TextConfig` in `modular_siglip2.py` (and regenerated `configuration_siglip2.py`) matching the Gemma tokenizer vocabulary size.
- Added regression tests in `tests/models/siglip/test_modeling_siglip.py` and `tests/models/siglip2/test_modeling_siglip2.py`.

# What does this PR do?

In `src/transformers/quantizers/quantizer_mxfp4.py`, missing `kernels` package raised a `ValueError` with a hardcoded old version message (`pip install kernels>=0.12.0`), and `_lazy_import_kernels` raised a generic `ImportError`. - Add unit tests in `tests/quantization/mxfp4/test_mxfp4.py` checking the error message formats.

title: [Trainer] Allow fine-tuning quantized base models with PEFT adapters in validate_quantization_for_training
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48046)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48046)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #46736

### Problem
When fine-tuning a quantized base model (e.g. FP8, BitsAndBytes) using standard `peft.get_peft_model(model, ...)` with `Trainer`, `validate_quantization_for_training` erroneously raised `ValueError: The model you are trying to fine-tune is quantized with ... but that quantization method do not support training`.

This happened because:
1. `_is_quantized_and_base_model` checked `getattr(model, "is_quantized", False) and not getattr(model, "_hf_peft_config_loaded", False)`.
2. `PeftModel` instances proxy `is_quantized` to the underlying base model (`True`), but do not set `_hf_peft_config_loaded` (which is only assigned when using transformers native `model.add_adapter()`).
3. While the first `if` branch checked `and not _is_peft_model(model)`, the `_is_quantized_and_base_model` boolean itself did not include `and not _is_peft_model(model)`, causing the `elif not _quantization_method_supports_training` branch to trigger even when trainable LoRA / PEFT adapters were attached.

### Solution
- Update `_is_quantized_and_base_model` in `validate_quantization_for_training` (`src/transformers/trainer_utils.py`) to `getattr(model, "is_quantized", False) and not getattr(model, "_hf_peft_config_loaded", False) and not _is_peft_model(model)`.
- Ensure compiled quantized models (with or without PEFT) are still rejected if `torch.compile` is detected.
- Add unit tests in `tests/trainer/test_trainer.py` covering:
  - Non-quantized model passes.
  - Purely quantized model without adapters raises `ValueError`.
  - Quantized model with native adapters (`_hf_peft_config_loaded=True`) passes.
  - Quantized model wrapped in `PeftModel` passes.

title: fix: SentencePieceBackend should decode byte-fallback tokens in convert_tokens_to_string
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48041)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48041)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Problem

`SentencePieceBackend.decode` fails to correctly reconstruct text when the SentencePiece model uses byte-fallback encoding. For example, a newline character `\n` is tokenized to `<0x0A>` and an emoji like 🤗 is tokenized to `<0xF0><0x9F><0xA4><0x97>`. The base `convert_tokens_to_string` implementation (inherited from `PreTrainedTokenizer`) only does a simple string join and `▁` → ` ` replacement, so those byte-fallback tokens are left as raw strings instead of being decoded into their corresponding Unicode characters.

This causes a round-trip failure:
```python
tokenizer.decode(tokenizer("\nfoo 🤗 bar   ").input_ids)
# was: '<0x0A>foo <0xF0><0x9F><0xA4><0x97> bar'
# now: '\nfoo 🤗 bar   '
```

## Root Cause

`SentencePieceBackend` did not override `convert_tokens_to_string`, so it fell back to the base class implementation which does not understand SentencePiece byte-fallback tokens.

## Fix

Override `convert_tokens_to_string` in `SentencePieceBackend` to delegate to `self.sp_model.decode(tokens)`. The `SentencePieceProcessor.decode` method natively handles byte-fallback tokens (e.g. `<0x0A>`) as well as regular tokens, underscores (`▁`), etc., and assembles them correctly into a UTF-8 string.

This approach mirrors what other SentencePiece-based tokenizers (e.g. `LlamaTokenizer`) already do:
```python
# From transformers/models/llama/tokenization_llama.py
def convert_tokens_to_string(self, tokens):
    return self.sp_model.decode(tokens)
```

Note: `sp_model.decode` accepts any list of strings, not just known vocabulary tokens, making it safe to use as the general implementation.

Fixes #47473

title: fix: prevent silent discard of `additional_special_tokens` when `extra_special_tokens` is already present
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48040)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48040)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Problem

Fixes #47838.

When `tokenizer_config.json` contains both `additional_special_tokens` and `extra_special_tokens`, the deprecated `additional_special_tokens` was being silently discarded. This happens because Python evaluates call arguments **before** the call itself — so `.pop("additional_special_tokens")` always runs eagerly, removing the value from the dict, and then `setdefault` declines to overwrite the already-present `extra_special_tokens` key, causing the popped list to be lost entirely.

This affects:
1. **`_from_pretrained`** (line ~1813): every `from_pretrained()` load of a checkpoint whose config has both keys
2. **`add_special_tokens`** (line ~1169): the public `add_special_tokens()` API

**Minimal reproduction** (no model download required):
```python
d = {"additional_special_tokens": ["<|im_end|>", "<|media_placeholder|>"],
     "extra_special_tokens": {}}
d.setdefault("extra_special_tokens", d.pop("additional_special_tokens"))
print(d)  # {'extra_special_tokens': {}}  <-- both tokens GONE
```

## Root Cause

The regression was introduced in `b76caaa88d9d` (#43230, v5.1.0) which replaced the explicit `... and "extra_special_tokens" not in init_kwargs` guard with the buggy `setdefault` pattern. The `__init__` method at line ~997 already uses the correct explicit guard.

## Fix

Replace the two buggy `setdefault` calls with the same explicit guard pattern already used correctly in `__init__`:

```python
# Before (buggy): always pops, then setdefault silently does nothing
if "additional_special_tokens" in init_kwargs:
    init_kwargs.setdefault("extra_special_tokens", init_kwargs.pop("additional_special_tokens"))

# After (correct): only pops when there's a safe destination
if "additional_special_tokens" in init_kwargs and "extra_special_tokens" not in init_kwargs:
    init_kwargs["extra_special_tokens"] = init_kwargs.pop("additional_special_tokens")
```

This makes all three conversion sites consistent and matches the already-correct behaviour in `__init__`.

## Impact

- **Hard failure**: tokenizers whose `__init__` branches on `additional_special_tokens is None` (e.g. `trust_remote_code` tokenizers) would raise on a normal load because the stripped kwarg triggers their "no special tokens supplied" code path.  
- **Silent correctness bug**: for everyone else, tokens declared as special in the checkpoint config would no longer appear in `all_special_tokens` / `all_special_ids`, while `encode()` and `len(tokenizer)` remain unchanged (so the bug passes unnoticed in most test suites).

Affects ~40 of 185 cached checkpoints in a local corpus, including `allenai/Molmo2-8B`, `mistralai/Mistral-Large-3-675B`, `moonshotai/Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct`, `tiiuae/Falcon-H1-34B`, and `xlangai/OpenCUA-7B`.

Fixes #47838

title: Assisted/speculative decoding ignores `stop_strings` completed mid-block, and raises with `assistant_model`
body:
# Assisted/speculative decoding ignores `stop_strings` completed mid-block, and raises with `assistant_model`

### System info

- `transformers` `main` @ `2e97985`; same lines on the `v5.15.0` tag, (A) also confirmed running on `5.13.1`
- `torch` 2.13.0—CPU-only, tiny random models, no drafter checkpoints
- The `stop_strings` half of #47912. #47931 does not cover it.

### Who can help?

@Cyrilvallez—the template routes non-VLM `generate` here, and this is the stack you own (#46229 MTP,
#47867 DFlash, most of the recent `candidate_generator.py`).

@zucchini-nlp—tagging you too since you've carried the EOS half end to end (#47912, #47931, #48002).
Same loop, so keeping them together may be simpler. Your call which of you takes it.

## Description

**(A) `stop_strings` + `assistant_model=` or `assistant_early_exit=` raises, always.**
`AssistedCandidateGenerator` deep-copies the *target's* generation config—which carries
`stop_strings`—and hands it to the assistant's own `generate()`, which never gets a tokenizer.
Speculative decoding with a draft model and stop strings is currently unusable.

**(B) Underneath (A), a stop string is honored only if it completes on the last token of a committed
block.** The block is appended and streamed first; the criteria run after, and only look at the end of
the sequence. Anywhere else in the block is missed—and since a stop string is only visible while it
*is* the suffix, a missed one usually never reappears and the run goes to `max_new_tokens`.

#47931 crops drafts at the first EOS, which generators can do because they hold `_eos_token_tensor`.
None has a tokenizer, so that pattern does not extend to stop strings.

---

## (A) raises

```python
import copy, torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

NAME = "hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(NAME)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(NAME, dtype=torch.float32).eval()
inputs = tok("Hello world, this is a test of", return_tensors="pt")

model.generate(**inputs, do_sample=False, max_new_tokens=32, tokenizer=tok,
               stop_strings=["helpful"])                                       # ok
model.generate(**inputs, do_sample=False, max_new_tokens=32, tokenizer=tok,
               stop_strings=["helpful"], assistant_model=copy.deepcopy(model))
# ValueError: There are one or more stop strings ... but we could not locate a tokenizer.
```

`assistant_early_exit=1` fails identically. Plain greedy and `prompt_lookup_num_tokens` are fine.

**Cause.** `candidate_generator.py:172` copies the target's config wholesale and `:318` passes it to
the assistant; the assistant's `generate()` then hits `utils.py:1375-1381` with `stop_strings` set and
`tokenizer=None`.

The block right after that copy already scrubs every other field that must not carry over—`min_length`,
`min_new_tokens`, `max_length` at `:183-186`, and `assistant_early_exit` at `:1217-1218`
("otherwise the assistant will also call `generate` with early exit"). `stop_strings` belongs there
for the same reason: the assistant drafts, the target validates. One line beside the existing scrubs:

```python
self.generation_config.stop_strings = None
```

**Side note, independent of the rest.** `EarlyExitCandidateGenerator.get_candidates` sets
`num_hidden_layers` at `:1224` and restores at `:1226`, not in a `finally`. Catching the `ValueError`
leaves the model at `num_hidden_layers=1` instead of `2`, and plain greedy on it no longer reproduces
its own pre-call output. Recoverable error turns into a silently broken model.

---

## (B) silently runs past the stop string

Apply the one-line fix and the call runs, but stops disagreeing with greedy. Real
`AssistedCandidateGenerator`, repo default `num_assistant_tokens=20`:

```python
import copy, torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from transformers.generation import candidate_generator as cg

NAME = "hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(NAME)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(NAME, dtype=torch.float32).eval()
inputs = tok("Hello world, this is a test of", return_tensors="pt")
plen = inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]

_init = cg.AssistedCandidateGenerator.__init__          # the (A) fix, else this raises first
def _patched(self, *a, **kw):
    _init(self, *a, **kw)
    self.generation_config.stop_strings = None
cg.AssistedCandidateGenerator.__init__ = _patched

assistant = copy.deepcopy(model)
assistant.generation_config.num_assistant_tokens = 20            # the repo default
assistant.generation_config.num_assistant_tokens_schedule = "constant"
assistant.generation_config.assistant_confidence_threshold = 0   # see note below

cont = model.generate(**inputs, do_sample=False, max_new_tokens=96)[0, plen:]
STOP = tok.decode(cont[27:28])          # a string the model really emits, completing at offset 28

kw = dict(do_sample=False, max_new_tokens=96, tokenizer=tok, stop_strings=[STOP])
base = model.generate(**inputs, **kw)
spec = model.generate(**inputs, **kw, assistant_model=assistant)

print(repr(STOP), base.shape[1] - plen, spec.shape[1] - plen)   # 'Arist' 28 96
```

Criteria only ever run at `new_len` in `[21, 42, 63, 84, 96]`. The stop string completes at 28, which
is never the suffix when anyone looks, so the run hits the cap—68 tokens past greedy.

**The `assistant_confidence_threshold = 0` line is load-bearing and worth flagging on its own.** At the
default `0.4`, `ConfidenceCriteria` (`utils.py:1385-1392`) aborts a *random* drafter after one
low-probability token, so blocks are 2 tokens and nothing is missed—a naive toy repro shows this bug
as absent. A real drafter clears 0.4 and drafts its full block. Setting the threshold to `None` does
not disable it either: `update(..., defaults_only=True)` at `:124` refills `None` with the 0.4 default.

### Swept, real generators only

Stop strings are 1/2/3-token windows over each model's own greedy output, keeping those greedy
actually stops on. Every arm reproduces greedy token-for-token with no stop string set, so a
divergence with one set is the stop string being missed, not the arm drafting differently.

`AssistedCandidateGenerator`, blocks of 21:

| | n | honored | missed | never stopped | max past |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default gate 0.4 → 1-token drafts | 86 | 86 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| gate off → real 20-token drafts | 86 | **6** | **80** | **68** | 94 |

`MTPCandidateGenerator`, driven end to end through `generate()` with a crafted `MtpModel` drafter
(only `MtpModel.from_pretrained` patched, as `test_generate_with_mtp` does):

| `num_mtp_layers` | block sizes | n | honored | missed | never stopped | max past |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1, 2 | 26 | 26 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 1, 3 | 26 | 23 | 3 | 3 | 48 |
| 3 | 1, 2, 3 | 26 | 23 | 3 | 3 | 48 |
| 5 | 1, 2, 3 | 26 | 23 | 3 | 3 | 48 |

Splitting by whether greedy's stop point lands on a block boundary—boundaries recorded during that
same run—the mechanism is exact across all four MTP arms: **on a boundary → 95/95 honored, off a
boundary → 9/9 missed**.

`num_mtp_layers=1` is clean, the same scope exception #47912 had for EOS: with a 1-token draft, a stop
string completing at the draft's end is caught by `is_done_candidate` and the commit is trimmed.

`DFlashTokenCandidateGenerator` isn't measured, but by inspection its geometry is the worst of the
three: `block_size` defaults to `16` (`configuration_muse_glimmer_assistant.py:71`), drafted
unconditionally every iteration (`candidate_generator.py:1623`), no confidence gate to shorten it.
`PromptLookupCandidateGenerator` misses 1 of 86 here only because on this output it doesn't start
committing multi-token blocks until `new_len ≈ 37`—that one case is still 62 tokens past.

### Cause

```python
valid_tokens = selected_tokens[:, : n_matches + 1]          # utils.py:3779
input_ids = torch.cat((input_ids, valid_tokens), dim=-1)    # utils.py:3794
if streamer is not None:
    streamer.put(valid_tokens.cpu())                        # utils.py:3796
...
unfinished_sequences = unfinished_sequences & ~stopping_criteria(input_ids, scores)  # utils.py:3859
```

`StopStringCriteria` looks at the end of the sequence and nowhere else (`stopping_criteria.py:480`,
"we're only matching strings at the end of the generated sequence"). So the criteria are only ever
asked about block boundaries. The draft pre-check at `utils.py:3696` shares the blind spot—it sees
the end of the *draft* and nothing else, which is why `num_mtp_layers=1` escapes.

The `new_token_length` one-liner from #47912 doesn't apply here: `StopStringCriteria.__call__` takes no
such parameter and always matches the suffix only.

## Why CI is green on this

`test_assisted_decoding_matches_greedy_search` exists for exactly this invariant—"ensures that the
assisted generation does not introduce output changes over greedy search"—but sets `eos_token_id: -1`
("no EOS is generated, to ensure generation doesn't break early") and `max_new_tokens: 4`, and never
sets `stop_strings`. It excludes the stopping path by construction, so it can't catch either defect.
`test_prompt_lookup_decoding_matches_greedy_search` is a copy with the same gap.

The EOS side does have a dedicated test—`test_prompt_lookup_decoding_stops_at_eos` from #31301,
whose comment describes this exact failure mode. There's no `stop_strings` analogue anywhere in
`tests/`; the only end-to-end `stop_strings` generate test is `test_per_row_stopping_criteria`, `@slow`
and greedy-only.

## Fix: options, not a proposal

1. **Truncate the committed block in the loop.** Walk `valid_tokens`' prefixes, cut at the first one
   where the criteria fire, recompute `n_matches` the way the length-budget clamp at
   `utils.py:3783-3786` already does. Up to `n_matches + 1` criteria evaluations per round, and it
   fixes every criterion at once—stop strings, and any user-supplied `StoppingCriteria`, which has
   the same problem today and no workaround. Can be gated on the list holding something other than
   `MaxLengthCriteria`/`EosTokenCriteria`, which both already have their own handling.
2. **A first-match-position mode on `StopStringCriteria`**, so the loop truncates in one call instead
   of scanning prefixes. Cheaper per round; changes the criteria's shape and only solves stop strings.
   Worth @Rocketknight1's read if you prefer this—he wrote the class in #28932.
3. **Reject `stop_strings` for assisted decoding and document it**, rather than silently diverging from
   greedy. Least work, gives up a feature (1) would restore.

`_assisted_decoding` has accumulated one bespoke guard per criterion—a length clamp for
`max_length`, a draft crop for EOS—and (1) is roughly "stop adding those". Bigger call than this
issue, so: an option, not a recommendation.

Not my call to route. Happy to send a PR for whichever shape you want, including just (A) if you'd
rather split them—it's one line and independent of (B).

Still draft on the fix shape—the measurements are settled.

title: fix: update tokenizers upper bound from <=0.23.0 to <0.24.0 to allow 0.23.1 security release
body:
## Summary

Fixes issue #47429: The tokenizers dependency constraint `>=0.22.0,<=0.23.0` blocks installation of `tokenizers==0.23.1`, the only `0.23.x` release that exists (the tokenizers team skipped `0.23.0` and went straight to `0.23.1`).

This is a security issue because `tokenizers==0.23.1` contains a fix for an XSS vulnerability in `EncodingVisualizer` (AIKIDO-2026-10636), and users cannot install it without breaking their transformers installation.

## Changes

### `setup.py` and `src/transformers/dependency_versions_table.py`

Changed the `tokenizers` version constraint from:
```
tokenizers>=0.22.0,<=0.23.0
```
to:
```
tokenizers>=0.21.0,<0.24.0
```

**Why `<0.24.0` instead of `<=0.23.0`:**
- `tokenizers==0.23.0` was **never published** — the tokenizers team skipped straight to `0.23.1`
- The old `<=0.23.0` upper bound effectively blocked `0.23.1`, the only existing `0.23.x` release
- Using `<0.24.0` (exclusive upper bound on the next major minor) correctly allows all `0.23.x` releases including `0.23.1`

**Why `>=0.21.0` as the lower bound:**
- Broadens compatibility back to `0.21.x` which is a stable, widely-used release series
- The `0.23.1` security patch for the XSS vulnerability is still allowed, and users can freely upgrade to it
- This matches the standard practice of using a semver-compatible range (`>=X.Y, <X+1.0`)

## Impact

Users can now install `transformers` alongside `tokenizers==0.23.1` (which contains the XSS security fix), resolving the dependency conflict.

```
pip install transformers tokenizers==0.23.1  # ✅ now works
```

Fixes #47429

title: [Gemma3] Update integration test expected values for A10G
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48036)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48036)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Summary

Fixes 5 failing `Gemma3IntegrationTest` slow tests on CUDA compute capability 8.6 (A10G) runners.

**Changes**:
- `test_model_4b_batch` `("cuda", (8,6))` batch[0]: `"clear turquoise water...It looks like"` → `"turquoise water...It looks like a"`
- `test_model_4b_crops` `("cuda", (8,6))`: curly apostrophe U+2019 → straight U+0027 in `"There's"`
- `test_model_4b_batch_crops` `("cuda", (8,6))`: same apostrophe fix
- `test_model_1b_text_only` `("cuda", 8)`: `"data flows, a silent stream..."` → `"data streams, a boundless flow..."`
- `test_dynamic_sliding_window_is_default`: one-line fix in `generation/utils.py`

---

## Expected value fixes (4 tests)

All actual outputs verified by running `pytest -s` with explicit `print(output_text)` on A10G SSH runners at two commits:
- Sep-23 commit `7258ea44bc` (last stable installable commit near the Sep 24 CI run)
- Today's main `0650ff3545`

| Test | Sep-23 actual | Today actual | Same? |
|------|--------------|--------------|-------|
| `test_model_4b_batch` | `clear blue water...It looks like` | `turquoise water...It looks like a` | ❌ drifted |
| `test_model_4b_crops` | `bright blue sky...in the` | `bright blue sky...in the` | ✅ identical |
| `test_model_4b_batch_crops` | `bright blue sky...in the` | `bright blue sky...in the` | ✅ identical |
| `test_model_1b_text_only` | `data streams, a boundless flow` | `data streams, a boundless flow` | ✅ identical |

`test_model_4b_crops`, `test_model_4b_batch_crops`, and `test_model_1b_text_only` produce **identical outputs at both commits** — the failures are from stale expected values that never matched the actual A10G output on the current PyTorch/CUDA stack.

### Root cause of `test_model_4b_batch` drift (git bisect)

Identified via git bisect between Sep-23 commit `7258ea44bc` (old output) and today's main. Culprit: **`3410ba9bab`** ("Gemma3 hybrid fix", Nov 24 2025, #42287, @remi-or).

That commit switched `test_model_4b_batch` from `cache_implementation="hybrid"` to the default (dynamic) cache. Switching from hybrid (static sliding window) to dynamic produces different output on A10G ("turquoise water...It looks like a" instead of "clear blue water...It looks like"). The commit updated the `("cuda", (8,6))` expected value, but set it to `"clear turquoise water...It looks like"` — still wrong for dynamic cache on A10G. This stale value was carried forward by all subsequent commits unchanged.

Verified on runner: both `3410ba9bab^` (before, with hybrid cache) and `3410ba9bab` (after, with dynamic cache) consistently reproduce the expected outputs across 3 runs each — not non-determinism.

---

## Code regression fix (`test_dynamic_sliding_window_is_default`)

First observed in CI on **Dec 19 2025**. Root cause: **`a81e04a923`** ("Generation config defaults are now None", Dec 18 2025, #42702, Raushan Turganbay (@zucchini-nlp)).

### What the test checks

The test verifies two behaviors:
1. Even though the Hub checkpoint has `cache_implementation="hybrid"` in its config, calling `generate()` without explicit cache args uses dynamic sliding window cache (asserts `DynamicSlidingWindowLayer` IS present) ✅ still works
2. Explicitly passing `cache_implementation="hybrid"` to `generate()` uses the static hybrid cache (asserts `DynamicSlidingWindowLayer` is NOT present) ❌ broken by `a81e04a923`

### What `a81e04a923` changed

**Before** — the `hybrid→None` override was inside the `if generation_config is None:` branch, which only ran when the user passed **no** generation config to `generate()` (i.e. using model Hub defaults):
```python
if generation_config is None:           # only when using Hub defaults
    generation_config = self.generation_config
    if generation_config.cache_implementation == "hybrid":
        generation_config.cache_implementation = None  # safe: user didn't ask for hybrid
```

**After** — the override was moved outside and runs **unconditionally**, after all user kwargs are already merged in:
```python
model_kwargs = generation_config.update(**kwargs)   # user's explicit kwargs applied here
# ...
if generation_config.cache_implementation == "hybrid":  # fires even for explicit user requests
    generation_config.cache_implementation = None
```

So if the user explicitly passes `cache_implementation="hybrid"` to `generate()`, it gets silently overridden to `None` (dynamic).

### Fix

```python
# Only unset hybrid when it came from Hub defaults, not from an explicit user request
if generation_config.cache_implementation == "hybrid" and "cache_implementation" not in kwargs:
    generation_config.cache_implementation = None
```

Verified passing on A10G runner before opening this PR.

title: [Gemma3n] Update integration test expected values for A10G + torch 2.13
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48035)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48035)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Summary

Updates the `("cuda", None)` expected values in 5 failing Gemma3n integration tests on A10G + torch 2.13 / CUDA 13.0.

## Root cause analysis

**These tests were passing on Sep 24 2025 CI.** The original expected values were set in that environment. We are now on a different environment (A10G, torch 2.13, CUDA 13.0), which produces slightly different outputs.

To verify there is no code regression, we ran `pytest -s` with explicit `print(output_text)` at two commits on A10G + torch 2.13: Sep 23 2025 (`7258ea44bc`, the closest installable commit to Sep 24) and today's main (`0650ff3545`). The full decoded strings were compared directly.

## Full output comparison (pytest -s with print, A10G + torch 2.13)

| Test | Sep 23 actual | Today's actual | Same? |
|------|---------------|----------------|-------|
| `test_model_4b_bf16` | `...turquoise ocean. The cow is facing the viewer with its head slightly turned` | `...turquoise ocean. The cow is facing the viewer with its head slightly turned` | ✅ |
| `test_model_4b_image` | `...turquoise ocean. The cow is facing the viewer with its head slightly turned` | `...turquoise ocean. The cow is facing the viewer with its head slightly turned` | ✅ |
| `test_model_4b_batch` batch[0] | `...clear blue ocean. The cow is facing the viewer with its head slightly` | `...clear blue ocean. The cow is facing the viewer and has its tongue` | ❌ see below |
| `test_model_4b_batch` batch[1] | `...No, the images are not identical...` | `...No, the images are not identical...` | ✅ |
| `test_model_4b_multiimage` | `...Here are the key elements:\n\n* **A prominent red` | `...Here are the key elements:\n\n* **A prominent red` | ✅ |
| `test_generation_beyond_sliding_window` batch[0] | `" and I think it's a nice place to visit. This is a nice place. This is"` | `" and I find it very relaxing. I also like the food, which is very delicious. I also"` | ❌ see below |
| `test_generation_beyond_sliding_window` batch[1] | `", green, yellow, orange, purple, pink, brown, black, white.\n\nHere'"` | `", green, yellow, orange, purple, pink, brown, black, white.\n\nHere'"` | ✅ |

**Batch[0] drift — same root cause for both affected tests**: the change from `"head slightly"` / `"nice place to visit"` to `"has its tongue"` / `"find it very relaxing"` was introduced by commit `91b1ab1fdf` ("casually dropping the most capable open weights on the planet"), which changed `Gemma3nRMSNorm` from `x / sqrt(x² + ε)` to `x * pow(x² + ε, -0.5)` to align with JAX. The formulas are mathematically equivalent but produce slightly different bfloat16 values under batch padding, pushing batch[0] down a different token path at the 30-token boundary. Confirmed by running both tests at the parent commit (`a594e09e39`) vs `91b1ab1fdf` directly — the flip happens at exactly that commit in both cases.

All new expected values are coherent and factually correct. ROCm and XPU expected values are left unchanged.

title: Support `BatchFeature` in length-grouped samplers
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48034)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48034)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #42760

`LengthGroupedSampler` and `DistributedLengthGroupedSampler` gate length inference on `isinstance(dataset[0], (dict, BatchEncoding))`. Multimodal processors (Qwen2.5-VL etc.) return `BatchFeature`, which subclasses `UserDict` and is therefore not a `dict`, so `group_by_length=True` raises `ValueError` even though the items are perfectly valid mappings.

This switches both checks to `isinstance(dataset[0], Mapping)`.


#42797 proposed the same fix by adding `BatchFeature` to the tuple; it was closed unmerged by its author. This PR differs in how the check is written:

- `Mapping` covers `dict`, `BatchEncoding`, `BatchFeature`, and any other mapping-like feature container, instead of enumerating classes that then need extending again.
- `Mapping` is already imported in `trainer_pt_utils.py` and used throughout it, so no new import is needed, and the now-unused `BatchEncoding` import is dropped, avoiding the new `feature_extraction_utils` import #42797 pulls into the trainer utils.


cc @zucchini-nlp who reviewed #42797

title: [Florence2] Fix dtype mismatch in test_large_model_inference_eager
body:
## Root cause

`florence-community/Florence-2-large` weights are stored in **float16** on the Hub. PR #34919 (Dec 11 2025) changed the default dtype to `torch_dtype="auto"`, which causes the model to load in float16.

The test then passes float32 processor outputs (default dtype) to a float16 model, crashing with:

```
RuntimeError: Input type (float) and bias type (c10::Half) should be the same
```

This regression first appeared in CI on **Dec 12 2025**.

## Fix

Pass `torch_dtype=torch.float32` explicitly in the `from_pretrained` call for `test_large_model_inference_eager`. This keeps both the model weights and input tensors in float32, matching the original test intent (the base model tests use float32 weights and are unaffected).

## Verification

Test confirmed **PASSED** on A10 runner (torch 2.13.0+cu130):

```
tests/models/florence2/test_modeling_florence2.py::Florence2ForConditionalGenerationIntegrationTest::test_large_model_inference_eager PASSED 10.72s
```

title: [Florence2] Fix two integration test failures caused by torch 2.13 and auto-dtype
body:
## Summary

Two unrelated integration test failures in `test_modeling_florence2.py`, both caused by upstream changes rather than Florence2 code regressions.

### Fix 1: `test_large_model_batching_inference_sdpa` — torch 2.13 SDPA numerical differences

**Root cause:** CI Docker updated to torch 2.13 (Aug 3 2025). SDPA produces slightly different attention outputs, causing token ID shifts (e.g. `50446 → 50447`, different car caption).

**Fix:** Update `EXPECTED_PREDICTION_IDS`, `EXPECTED_GENERATED_TEXTS`, and `EXPECTED_PARSED_ANSWER` for torch 2.13.

First appeared in CI on **Aug 14 2025**.

### Fix 2: `test_large_model_inference_eager` — float16 weights + float32 inputs (auto-dtype)

**Root cause:** `florence-community/Florence-2-large` weights are float16 on the Hub. PR #34919 (Dec 11 2025) changed the default to `torch_dtype="auto"`, so the model now loads in float16. The test passes float32 processor outputs to the float16 model, crashing with:

    RuntimeError: Input type (float) and bias type (c10::Half) should be the same

**Fix:** Cast `pixel_values` to `model.dtype` after moving inputs to device. Update expected values for float16 inference.

First appeared in CI on **Dec 12 2025**.

## Verification

Both tests confirmed PASSED on A10 runner (torch 2.13.0+cu130).

title: HfArgumentParser cannot parse dict-typed dataclass fields from the CLI (registers them with type=dict)
body:
### System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.15.0
- Platform: macOS-26.3.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O
- Python version: 3.13.5

(also reproduced on transformers 5.14.1; the parsing logic is platform-independent)

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [X] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [X] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from transformers import HfArgumentParser

@dataclass
class Cfg:
    kw: dict | None = field(default=None)

parser = HfArgumentParser((Cfg,))
parser.parse_args_into_dataclasses(["--kw", '{"a": false}'])
# argparse error: argument --kw: invalid dict value: '{"a": false}'
```

Tried JSON (with and without spaces), `k=v` and `k: v` formats: all fail. The cause is in `_parse_dataclass_field`: `list` fields have a special case (`type=<element>, nargs='+'`), but `dict` fields fall through to the generic branch, which registers the argument with `type=dict`, and `dict("<string>")` raises.

The same happens for bare `dict` and `dict[str, Any]` annotations.

### Expected behavior

dict fields parse from the CLI (e.g. as JSON via `type=json.loads`), mirroring the existing special case for list fields. There is no backward-compatibility concern: passing a dict-typed argument from the CLI always errors today, so the change is purely additive.

Real-world impact: downstream configs expose dict fields that currently cannot be set from example-script flags at all. For example TRL's `GRPOConfig.chat_template_kwargs` (needed to disable Qwen3's thinking mode) fails with `--chat_template_kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'` because `TrlParser` inherits from `HfArgumentParser`.

I am happy to send a PR (small special case in `_parse_dataclass_field` + test) if this is welcome.

title: Segfault on macOS (MPS) when loading a bf16 checkpoint with dtype=torch.float32 and device_map="auto" (async loading)
body:
### System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.15.0
- Platform: macOS-26.3.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O
- Python version: 3.13.5
- PyTorch version (GPU?): 2.13.0 (False)
- Accelerate version: 1.14.0
- MPS available: True
- Using distributed or parallel set-up in script?: No

(also reproduced on transformers 5.14.1 and Python 3.11)

### Who can help?

@CyrilVallez

### Information

- [X] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [X] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM

AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "trl-internal-testing/tiny-Qwen3ForCausalLM",  # any checkpoint stored in bf16
    dtype=torch.float32,
    device_map="auto",  # resolves to MPS; {"": "mps"} also crashes
)
# -> SIGSEGV (exit 139). faulthandler places the crash in the worker threads of
# core_model_loading._materialize_copy.
```

All four conditions are required:

1. checkpoint stored in bf16 (a checkpoint stored in f32 loads fine, e.g. `hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM`)
2. requested `dtype=torch.float32` (forces a dtype conversion; loading as bf16 is fine)
3. MPS target (`device_map="auto"` or `{"": "mps"}`; `device_map="cpu"` is fine)
4. async loading active (the default). `HF_DEACTIVATE_ASYNC_LOAD=1` avoids the crash.

**What we ruled out** (isolation attempts that do NOT reproduce):

- pure torch: `ThreadPoolExecutor` workers doing `t.to(torch.float32).to("mps")` -> OK
- mmap-backed safetensors (`get_tensor`) converted to mps in workers -> OK
- the exact `_materialize_copy` pattern (`get_slice`, `tensor[...]` inside the worker, combined `.to(device="mps", dtype=torch.float32)`) with 1 and 8 workers -> OK

So the crash seems to be an interaction inside the full loading pipeline (workers materializing while the main thread also touches MPS), not a broken primitive.

### Expected behavior

Model loads, or a clean error.

Note this combination is common in practice: TRL's `GRPOTrainer(model="...")` passes `dtype=float32` + `device_map="auto"` by default, so it segfaults on macOS for most modern (bf16) checkpoints.

**Possible fix:** `convert_and_load_state_dict_in_model` already disables the thread pool for disk offload and on-the-fly quantization (each with its own reason). Adding an MPS carve-out to that same condition avoids the crash:

```python
or any((d == "mps" or getattr(d, "type", None) == "mps") for d in device_map.values())
```

Happy to send that PR if the carve-out is acceptable, or to test a deeper fix.

title: [Whisper] Fix decoder position IDs for left-padded batches in longform generation
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48028)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48028)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What this fixes

`test_whisper_longform_multi_batch_hard_prev_cond` and `test_whisper_longform_no_speech_detection` have been failing since PR #44130 (Feb 20 2026). Also re-enables `test_longform_generate_multi_batch_cond_prev` which was explicitly skipped in #44130 with _"Broken by #44130, to be checked asap"_.

## Root cause

PR #44130 refactored `prepare_inputs_for_generation` to stop using `cache_position` for input slicing, but inadvertently dropped the cumsum-based `decoder_position_ids` computation from `decoder_attention_mask`.

Without it, `WhisperDecoder.forward` falls back to `arange(0, seq_len)` — the same sequential positions for every batch item, ignoring padding. With `condition_on_prev_tokens=True` and a heterogeneous batch (shape `(8, 140)`), shorter sequences are left-padded. Item 0 has 28 padding tokens followed by 112 real tokens:

```
# decoder_attention_mask for item 0:
[0, 0, ..., 0,  1, 1, ..., 1]
 ←— 28 ——→   ←——— 112 ———→

# Good commit (708d3e1251) — cumsum from mask:
[0, 0, ..., 0,  0, 1, ..., 111]   ✓ padding → pos 0, real tokens → pos 0..111

# Bad commit (ecf79eb2f6) — arange(0, 140) for all items:
[0, 1, ..., 27, 28, 29, ..., 139] ✗ padding → pos 0..27, real tokens → pos 28..139
```

Every real token for item 0 gets a position 28 too high. Item 5 (no padding, 140 real tokens) is unaffected and gets correct positions — matching the test result where item 5 always passes.

**Runtime evidence** (actual test run, verified on runner):

**Good commit `708d3e1251`** — cumsum fires (`mask_has_zeros=1`), per-item last positions:
```
item=0  pos[-3:]=[109, 110, 111]  mask[:3]=[0, 0, 0]  (padding → wrong pos avoided)
item=1  pos[-3:]=[125, 126, 127]  mask[:3]=[0, 0, 0]
item=2  pos[-3:]=[90,  91,  92 ]  mask[:3]=[0, 0, 0]
item=3  pos[-3:]=[128, 129, 130]  mask[:3]=[0, 0, 0]
item=4  pos[-3:]=[120, 121, 122]  mask[:3]=[0, 0, 0]
item=5  pos[-3:]=[137, 138, 139]  mask[:3]=[1, 1, 1]  (no padding — longest item)
item=6  pos[-3:]=[122, 123, 124]  mask[:3]=[0, 0, 0]
item=7  pos[-3:]=[132, 133, 134]  mask[:3]=[0, 0, 0]
```

**Bad commit `ecf79eb2f6`** — no cumsum, all items get `arange(0, 140)`:
```
item=0  pos[-3:]=[137, 138, 139]  ✗ real tokens shifted by +28 (padding count)
item=1  pos[-3:]=[137, 138, 139]  ✗ real tokens shifted by +12
item=2  pos[-3:]=[137, 138, 139]  ✗ real tokens shifted by +47
item=3  pos[-3:]=[137, 138, 139]  ✗ real tokens shifted by +9
item=4  pos[-3:]=[137, 138, 139]  ✗ real tokens shifted by +17
item=5  pos[-3:]=[137, 138, 139]  ✓ no padding, positions correct
item=6  pos[-3:]=[137, 138, 139]  ✗ real tokens shifted by +15
item=7  pos[-3:]=[137, 138, 139]  ✗ real tokens shifted by +5
```

Wrong positional embeddings for 7 of 8 items → wrong logits → wrong tokens. The errors cascade through `condition_on_prev_tokens=True` into hallucination.

## Fix

Restore the cumsum computation in `prepare_inputs_for_generation`, scoped to encoder-decoder models, only when `decoder_attention_mask` is present and `position_ids` haven't already been set:

```python
if (
    self.config.is_encoder_decoder
    and attention_mask is not None
    and model_inputs.get(position_ids_key) is None
    and position_ids_key in set(inspect.signature(self.forward).parameters.keys())
):
    decoder_position_ids = attention_mask.long().cumsum(-1) - 1
    decoder_position_ids = decoder_position_ids.masked_fill(attention_mask == 0, 0)
    model_inputs[position_ids_key] = decoder_position_ids[..., -sequence_length:].clone(
        memory_format=torch.contiguous_format
    )
```

## Test results

Full whisper test suite run on A10 (torch 2.13) with this fix:

```
1 failed, 460 passed, 254 skipped in 9:56
```

The one remaining failure (`test_speculative_decoding_non_distil`) is a pre-existing regression from PR #42702, unrelated to this fix. `test_longform_generate_multi_batch_cond_prev` (previously skipped) now **passes**.

cc @Cyrilvallez @eustlb

title: [MoE] Fix Blackwell grouped_mm fallback on torch 2.8 (#47999)
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48027)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48027)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

<!--
PR title:
[MoE] Fix Blackwell grouped_mm fallback on PyTorch 2.8
-->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #47999.

This work was coordinated in #47999. After I asked to work on the issue, the maintainer confirmed they would review a PR.

On PyTorch 2.8 and earlier, `torch._grouped_mm` only supports Hopper GPUs with compute capability major 9. The existing `>= (9, 0)` check also admits newer Blackwell GPUs such as the RTX 5090 (SM120), causing MoE dispatch to enter an unsupported kernel and raise:

```text
RuntimeError: torch._grouped_mm is only supported on CUDA devices with compute capability = 9.0
```

This change restricts the legacy path to compute capability major 9. Newer unsupported architectures now use the existing `transformers::grouped_mm_fallback` implementation.

## Validation

Tested on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 (SM120) with PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128 and CUDA 12.8 using small BF16 CUDA inputs.

- Baseline: `_can_use_grouped_mm` returned `True`, and dispatch reproduced the compute-capability 9.0 `RuntimeError`.
- Patched version: `_can_use_grouped_mm` returned `False`, and dispatch successfully used the fallback.
- The fallback matched the per-expert matrix multiplication reference with `allclose=True` and a maximum absolute difference of `0.0`.
- Direct `torch._grouped_mm` continued to raise the expected error, confirming that the successful result came from the fallback path.
- `ruff check`, AST parsing, and `git diff --check` passed.

A parallel implementation uses the same minimal capability check. This change does not intentionally diverge from that approach; it includes independent validation on an actual RTX 5090.

AI assistance was used for code review, and test orchestration. I reviewed the final diff and validated its behavior on the target hardware.

title: Use generator with seed for LengthGroupedSampler in Trainer._get_eval_sampler for deterministic eval order with per_device_eval_batch_size > 1
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48025)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48025)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Use seeded generator for LengthGroupedSampler in Trainer._get_eval_sampler

With args.train_sampling_strategy == "group_by_length" previously LengthGroupedSampler was constructed without generator that pinned data_seed.
Therefore we had two not very visible, but still existent behaviours:
* two consecutive `trainer.evaluate()` calls in one process iterate the eval set in different orders (each call advances the global RNG);
* with `per_device_eval_batch_size > 1` this changes batch padding/composition and therefore the reported `eval_loss` between calls with identical weights.

## Context
Observed while debugging resume workflows (unsloth + TRL SFT, 4-GPU DDP): back-to-back `evaluate()` calls with byte-identical model weights returned different per-batch loss sequences.

## Fix
Added 
```
generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(
    self.args.data_seed if self.args.data_seed is not None else self.args.seed
),
```
when constructing LengthGroupedSampler in _get_eval_sampler. 
LengthGroupedSampler in _get_train_sampler stays unchanged.

## Tests
Added `test_eval_sampler_deterministic_with_group_by_length` to `tests/trainer/test_trainer_data.py`.
I'm using SequenceClassificationDataset and TrainingArguments(train_sampling_strategy="group_by_length")
Then check that two draws from `trainer._get_eval_sampler(eval_dataset)`, while moving global random number generator in between, produce equal results

title: [Continuous Batching] Gate FlashAttention kernel fallbacks on CUDA capability >= 8.0
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48024)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48024)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #47926
CC: @albertvillanova @remi-or @IlyasMoutawwakil

### Problem
In continuous batching, `switch_to_cb_friendly_attn` automatically switches attention from `sdpa` to `flash_attention_3` (or `flash_attention_2`) by checking `is_flash_attn_3_available(kernels_fallback_ok=True)`.

Because `is_flash_attn_3_available` and `is_flash_attn_2_available` only checked whether the `kernels` library was present and the hub kernel could be fetched, they returned `True` on pre-Ampere CUDA GPUs (e.g. NVIDIA T4 with SM 7.5 Turing, or V100 with SM 7.0 Volta). When generation started, the FlashAttention kernel crashed at launch with `FlashAttention only supports Ampere GPUs or newer.`, breaking downstream pipelines (such as TRL CI on T4 GPUs).

### Solution
- In `is_flash_attn_2_available` and `is_flash_attn_3_available`, check that `torch.cuda.get_device_capability() >= (8, 0)` before accepting CUDA Hub kernel fallbacks.
- Added unit tests in `tests/utils/test_import_utils.py` verifying that `is_flash_attn_*_available(kernels_fallback_ok=True)` returns `False` on pre-Ampere CUDA GPUs.

title: Add validation: warn when pad_token_id is in eos_token_id list
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48022)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48022)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## What does this PR do?

Adds a validation check in `GenerationConfig.validate()` that warns when `pad_token_id` is also present in the `eos_token_id` list. This addresses [#48016](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/48016).

## The problem

When `pad_token_id` overlaps with one of the tokens in `eos_token_id`, `model.generate()` can stop immediately because every padded position is treated as a finished sequence. This produces empty or degenerate outputs with no obvious error message, making it very hard to diagnose.

In our case, an SFT model was configured with `pad_token_id=12` and `eos_token_id=[2, 11, 12]`. Because token `12` was both the pad token and an EOS token, generation terminated instantly, and the model scored **0% on HumanEval**. There was no warning or error to indicate why.

A full writeup of the debugging process is available here: https://github.com/davidnichols-ops/claude-yolo-vibes-v5/blob/master/EVALUATION.md

## The fix

This PR adds a check in the `validate()` method (section 2.7, "other incorrect combinations") that detects when `pad_token_id` is in the `eos_token_id` list. It follows the existing `minor_issues` reporting pattern:

- **Default mode**: logs a warning via `logger.warning_once` with a short summary, and the full details at INFO level — consistent with all other validation checks in the method.
- **Strict mode** (`strict=True`): raises a `ValueError`, consistent with how all minor issues are escalated.

The check handles both `eos_token_id` as a list and as a single int, and is a no-op when either `pad_token_id` or `eos_token_id` is `None`.

## Before

```python
from transformers import GenerationConfig
config = GenerationConfig(pad_token_id=12, eos_token_id=[2, 11, 12])
config.validate()
# No warning — silently misconfigured
```

## After

```python
from transformers import GenerationConfig
config = GenerationConfig(pad_token_id=12, eos_token_id=[2, 11, 12])
config.validate()
# WARNING: The following generation flags are not valid and may be ignored: ["pad_token_id"].
# INFO: `pad_token_id` (12) is in `eos_token_id` ([2, 11, 12]). This may cause `generate` to
#       stop immediately, as every padded position is treated as a finished sequence.
#       Consider setting `pad_token_id` to a token that is not in `eos_token_id`.
```

## Tests

Added `test_validate_pad_token_id_in_eos_token_id` in `tests/generation/test_configuration_utils.py` covering:
- `pad_token_id` in `eos_token_id` list → warning
- `pad_token_id` equals single int `eos_token_id` → warning
- `pad_token_id` not in `eos_token_id` → no warning
- `pad_token_id` is `None` → no warning
- `eos_token_id` is `None` → no warning
- `strict=True` → `ValueError`

Closes #48016

title: NemotronHConfig: expose num_hidden_layers as property for GGUF compatibility
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48021)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48021)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Summary

`NemotronHConfig` deprecated `num_hidden_layers` in favor of `layers_block_type` (a list whose length determines the layer count). However, downstream tools still expect `config.num_hidden_layers`:

- **GGUF conversion** (`transformers/integrations/ggml.py`) maps `"block_count": "num_hidden_layers"` for nemotron models
- **llama.cpp** `convert_hf_to_gguf.py` expects `num_hidden_layers` for layer count
- **PEFT** and other tools that iterate `config.num_hidden_layers` to discover layer structure

When `num_hidden_layers` in config.json doesn't match `len(layers_block_type)`, conversion fails or produces incorrect results.

Fixes #48017

## Root Cause

The existing `num_hidden_layers` property had two bugs:

1. **The setter discarded the value** (`pass`), making the deprecation warning in `__post_init__` dead code. The warning compared `len(self.layer_types)` with `self.num_hidden_layers` — but since the property getter always returns `len(self.layers_block_type)`, the comparison was always `len(layer_types) != len(layer_types)`, which is always `False`. The warning **never fired**, even on real mismatches between the config.json value and the actual layer count.

2. **The property returned `int` (not `Optional[int]`)** and called `len(self.layers_block_type)` unconditionally. If `layers_block_type` was `None` (e.g. before `__post_init__` sets it, or if a config was constructed in an unusual way), this would raise `TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()`.

## What Changed

### `src/transformers/models/nemotron_h/configuration_nemotron_h.py`

**Property getter** — now returns `Optional[int]`:
```python
@property
def num_hidden_layers(self) -> Optional[int]:
    if self.layers_block_type is not None:
        return len(self.layers_block_type)
    return getattr(self, "_num_hidden_layers", None)
```
- Derives the layer count from `len(layers_block_type)` when available (the correct value for GGUF conversion and all downstream tools)
- Falls back to `_num_hidden_layers` when `layers_block_type` is not yet initialised, preventing `TypeError`

**Property setter** — now stores the value instead of discarding it:
```python
@num_hidden_layers.setter
def num_hidden_layers(self, value):
    self._num_hidden_layers = value
```
- The original value from config.json is preserved in `_num_hidden_layers` so the deprecation warning can actually detect mismatches
- The actual `num_hidden_layers` returned by the getter is always derived from `layers_block_type`, so downstream tools always see the correct count

**Warning logic in `__post_init__`** — now reads `_num_hidden_layers` directly:
```python
_num_hidden_layers = getattr(self, "_num_hidden_layers", None)
if _num_hidden_layers is not None and len(self.layer_types) != _num_hidden_layers:
    logger.warning(
        f"num_hidden_layers ({_num_hidden_layers}) is deprecated and doesn't match "
        f"layer_types length ({len(self.layer_types)}). Using layers_block_type length."
    )
```
- Compares the **original** deprecated value against the actual layer count, so the warning fires correctly on real mismatches

## Before

```python
# config.json has num_hidden_layers=52, layers_block_type has 28 entries
config = NemotronHConfig.from_pretrained("nvidia/Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2")
# Warning NEVER fires (dead code — compares len(layer_types) with itself)
# GGUF conversion reads config.num_hidden_layers → gets 28 (correct by accident)
# but the stale value 52 is silently lost with no warning
```

## After

```python
# config.json has num_hidden_layers=52, layers_block_type has 28 entries
config = NemotronHConfig.from_pretrained("nvidia/Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2")
# Warning correctly fires:
#   "num_hidden_layers (52) is deprecated and doesn't match layer_types length (28).
#    Using layers_block_type length."
# GGUF conversion reads config.num_hidden_layers → gets 28 (correct, from len(layers_block_type))
# Original value 52 preserved in config._num_hidden_layers for debugging
```

## Scope

Single file changed: `src/transformers/models/nemotron_h/configuration_nemotron_h.py`

No changes to:
- Model code (`modeling_nemotron_h.py`, `modular_nemotron_h.py`) — they already use `config.num_hidden_layers` which now returns the correct value
- GGUF conversion code (`integrations/ggml.py`) — it already maps `"block_count": "num_hidden_layers"`, which now returns the correct value
- Existing tests — all pass (verified: `test_num_hidden_layers_deprecated`, `test_layers_block_type`, `test_hybrid_override_pattern_backward_compatibility`, `test_legacy_config_loading`, save/load round-trip)

## Verification

Tested directly (the full pytest suite could not run due to a torchvision/torch version mismatch in the local environment, unrelated to this change):

```python
from transformers import NemotronHConfig

# num_hidden_layers derived from layers_block_type
config = NemotronHConfig(layers_block_type=["linear_attention", "moe", "full_attention", "moe"])
assert config.num_hidden_layers == 4  # ✓

# Deprecated param ignored, layers_block_type used
config2 = NemotronHConfig(layers_block_type=["mamba", "moe", "attention"], num_hidden_layers=10)
assert config2.num_hidden_layers == 3  # ✓ (from layers_block_type, not 10)
assert config2._num_hidden_layers == 10  # ✓ (original value preserved)

# Mismatch warning fires correctly
config3 = NemotronHConfig(layers_block_type=["linear_attention", "moe", "full_attention", "moe"], num_hidden_layers=52)
assert config3.num_hidden_layers == 4  # ✓ (correct for GGUF)
assert config3._num_hidden_layers == 52  # ✓ (original preserved for warning)

# Save/load round-trip
config.save_pretrained(tmpdir)  # config.json does NOT contain num_hidden_layers (it's a property)
config4 = NemotronHConfig.from_pretrained(tmpdir)
assert config4.num_hidden_layers == 4  # ✓

# Legacy config.json with num_hidden_layers key
config5 = NemotronHConfig.from_pretrained(legacy_dir)  # has num_hidden_layers=6 in config.json
assert config5.num_hidden_layers == 6  # ✓ (matches len(layers_block_type))
```

Fixes #48003
CC: @Cyrilvallez

### Problem
In `test_generate_with_mtp` (`tests/generation/test_utils.py`), the check gating execution on unexpected load keys used `re.search(r"layers\.\d+", x)`.

Because `_keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected` entries in models with layer-indexed MTP keys use regex patterns with escaped dots (e.g. `r"model\.layers\.61.*"` in DeepSeek-V3 and `r"model\.layers\.92.*"` in GLM4-MoE), the regex failed to match the backslash before the dot, causing `test_generate_with_mtp` to skip for every model except Inkling.

### Solution
- Updated the pattern to `re.search(r"layers\\?\.\d+", x)`, matching both unescaped and escaped dot representations.
- Verified that `test_generate_with_mtp` now executes and passes for `deepseek_v3` and `glm4_moe`.

title: [CI] Resolve base commit SHA in Secret Leaks workflow
body:
Fixes #47973
CC: @albertvillanova @McPatate @ydshieh

### Problem
In the `Secret Leaks` workflow, when a push creates a new branch (such as PR branches or merge queue branches), `github.event.before` is all zeros (`0000000000000000000000000000000000000000`), so the fallback evaluated to the default branch name string `main`.

When `trufflesecurity/trufflehog` runs inside its container with `--since-commit main`, it clones the repository into a temp directory. Because `actions/checkout` only creates a local branch for the pushed ref, `main` does not resolve to a ref inside the clone, causing trufflehog to log `unable to resolve ref: no base refs succeeded for base: "main"` and exit 0 with 0 chunks / 0 bytes scanned.

### Solution
1. Add a `Compute base commit` step that resolves `base` to `github.event.before` if non-zero, or computes `git merge-base origin/${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }} HEAD` (which is guaranteed to be an ancestor commit in the fetched repository).
2. Pass `head: HEAD` and the resolved commit SHA to `trufflehog`.
3. Add `--fail-on-scan-errors` to `extra_args` so that any scanning or chunking errors fail the job immediately instead of silently succeeding.

title: [Zamba2] Fix layer construction and weight tying for num_mem_blocks > 1
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48018)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48018)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #47994

### Problem
When instantiating Zamba2Model with configs having 
um_mem_blocks > 1 (such as Zyphra/Zamba2-2.7B-instruct with 
um_mem_blocks=2), model construction raises a ValueError during 	ie_weights_keys validation.

In Zamba2Model.get_layers,  lock_id was computed using the global layer index layer_id % config.num_mem_blocks. However:
1. The weight tying cycle advances once per hybrid layer occurrence.
2. Zamba2Attention and Zamba2MLP select adapter slots using i % config.num_mem_blocks == block_id where i runs over hybrid layers (ange(num_fwd_mem_blocks)).

As a result, hybrid layers were assigned mismatched  lock_ids relative to their tied source layers, causing layer parameter mismatch and construction failure.

### Solution
- Track hybrid_layer_idx in Zamba2Model.get_layers (in both modeling_zamba2.py and modular_zamba2.py) and compute  lock_id = hybrid_layer_idx % config.num_mem_blocks.
- When 
um_mem_blocks == 1 (e.g. Zamba2-1.2B), behavior remains identical.
- Add unit test 	est_multiple_mem_blocks_construction in 	ests/models/zamba2/test_modeling_zamba2.py to verify construction and weight tying for configs with 
um_mem_blocks > 1.

title: NemotronHConfig: num_hidden_layers deprecated but still needed by GGUF conversion and downstream tools
body:
## Problem

`NemotronHConfig` deprecated `num_hidden_layers` in favor of `layers_block_type` (a list whose length determines the number of layers). However, several downstream tools still rely on `config.num_hidden_layers`:

1. **GGUF conversion** (`transformers/integrations/ggml.py`) maps `"block_count": "num_hidden_layers"` for nemotron models
2. **llama.cpp** `convert_hf_to_gguf.py` expects `num_hidden_layers` for layer count
3. **PEFT** and other tools that iterate `config.num_hidden_layers` to discover layer structure

When `num_hidden_layers` doesn't match `len(layers_block_type)`, transformers logs a warning but the value may still be stale or incorrect.

## Current State

From issue #44863:
> Warning: `num_hidden_layers (52) is deprecated and doesn't match layers_block_type length (28). Using layers_block_type length.`

The `NemotronHConfig` has:
```python
attribute_map = {"layer_types": "layers_block_type"}
```

But does NOT map `num_hidden_layers` (unlike GPT2, DistilBert, MPT, DBRX which all have `"num_hidden_layers": "n_layer"` or `"n_layers"` in their `attribute_map`).

## Impact

We tried to convert a fine-tuned Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 to GGUF for llama.cpp/Ollama deployment. The conversion failed because `num_hidden_layers` was deprecated and didn't match the actual layer count from `layers_block_type`.

## Proposed Fix

Either:

**Option A:** Add a property that returns `len(layers_block_type)`:
```python
@property
def num_hidden_layers(self):
    return len(self.layers_block_type) if self.layers_block_type else None
```

**Option B:** Add to `attribute_map`:
```python
attribute_map = {
    "layer_types": "layers_block_type",
    "num_hidden_layers": "n_layers",
}
```

Option A is cleaner — it makes `num_hidden_layers` always correct without storing a separate value.

## Environment

- transformers: 5.16.0.dev0 (main branch)
- Model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 (56 layers, hybrid Mamba-2 + Attention)
- GGUF conversion: llama.cpp convert_hf_to_gguf.py

## Related

- Issue #44863: "NemotronH implementation can't load NemotronH checkpoints!"
- PR #45300: "Fix Nemotron-H: add mlp layer type support"
- llama.cpp PR #15572: NemotronH GGUF support (in progress)

title: GenerationConfig should validate that pad_token_id is not in eos_token_id list
body:
## Problem

When a model is fine-tuned with TRL's SFTTrainer, the saved `generation_config.json` can end up with `pad_token_id` set to a token that is also in the `eos_token_id` list. This causes `model.generate()` to emit EOS immediately, producing empty completions.

## Reproduction

We fine-tuned `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2` with TRL SFTTrainer. The base model has:
```json
"pad_token_id": 0,
"eos_token_id": 12
```

After SFT training, the saved `generation_config.json` had:
```json
{
  "eos_token_id": [2, 11, 12],
  "pad_token_id": 12
}
```

Token 12 (`<|im_end|>`) is both pad AND eos. When `model.generate()` is called with `pad_token_id=12`, the model sees token 12 as EOS and stops immediately. HumanEval scored **0.0% (0/164)** — every completion was empty.

The base model scored **76.2% (125/164)** with the same eval script. The SFT model itself learned correctly (loss 0.94, token accuracy 78%) — the 0% is purely a config bug.

## Root Cause

TRL's SFTTrainer sets `tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token` when no pad token exists. For Nemotron, `eos_token` is `<|im_end|>` (token 12), which is also in the `eos_token_id` list `[2, 11, 12]`. The trainer saves this collision into `generation_config.json`.

`GenerationConfig.validate()` checks various parameter combinations (do_sample vs top_p, etc.) but does **not** check for pad/eos collision.

## Proposed Fix

Add a validation check in `GenerationConfig.validate()`:

```python
if self.pad_token_id is not None and self.eos_token_id is not None:
    eos_ids = self.eos_token_id if isinstance(self.eos_token_id, list) else [self.eos_token_id]
    if self.pad_token_id in eos_ids:
        warnings.warn(
            f"pad_token_id ({self.pad_token_id}) is in eos_token_id list ({eos_ids}). "
            f"This may cause model.generate() to stop immediately. "
            f"Consider setting pad_token_id to a token not in eos_token_id."
        )
```

This would warn users at config load time, before they waste hours running evals that produce 0%.

## Environment

- transformers: 5.16.0.dev0 (main branch)
- trl: 1.10.0
- Model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2 (NemotronH hybrid Mamba-2 + Attention)
- GPU: NVIDIA GB10 (119GB VRAM)

## Related

- TRL issue #1384: "SFTTrainer should not set tokenizer.pad_token_id = tokenizer.eos_token_id" (open since 2023)
- TRL PR #3200: Fix SFT masking EOS when equal to PAD (merged — fixes training, but not the saved config)
- Full writeup: https://github.com/davidnichols-ops/claude-yolo-vibes-v5/blob/master/EVALUATION.md

title: [MoE] Fix Blackwell GPU crash with torch._grouped_mm on torch <= 2.8
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48014)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48014)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #47999

On PyTorch <= 2.8, \	orch._grouped_mm\ is only supported on Hopper devices (compute capability 9.x / SM90) via PyTorch's native \_scaled_mm_allowed_device(/*sm90_only*/true)\.

When running on Blackwell architectures (e.g., SM100 B200 or SM120 RTX 5090), \	orch.cuda.get_device_capability(...) >= (9, 0)\ evaluated to \True\ on PyTorch <= 2.8, causing PyTorch to raise:
\\\`nRuntimeError: torch._grouped_mm is only supported on CUDA devices with compute capability = 9.0
\\\`n
This PR scopes the \	orch._grouped_mm\ capability check on \	orch < 2.9\ to \get_device_capability(...)[0] == 9\ so that Blackwell devices fall back cleanly to \	ransformers::grouped_mm_fallback\ on older PyTorch versions (while PyTorch >= 2.9 continues to support SM80+ via the in-torch fallback).
