title: Fix EOS for candidate generators
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47931)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47931)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# Fix EOS for candidate generators

Fixes #47912. MTP folded in from #48002 per @zucchini-nlp's
[request](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/48002#issuecomment-5313657227) — one commit per
generator, same crop in both, mirroring `PromptLookupCandidateGenerator` (`candidate_generator.py:1134`).

## The bug

`_assisted_decoding` commits `n_matches + 1` tokens per round, appending and streaming the whole block
*before* the stopping criteria run, and `EosTokenCriteria` only inspects the last `new_token_length=1`
tokens. So an EOS accepted anywhere but the end of a block is missed and generation runs past it. It looks
intermittent because an EOS landing on the bonus token stops correctly. Block proposers hit it routinely —
DFlash drafts `block_size` (16) at a time, MTP drafts `num_mtp_layers`.

## Why cropping the draft is enough

`n_matches` is the leading run where the target's argmax equals the drafted token (`utils.py:3774`), and
`valid_tokens = selected_tokens[:, : n_matches + 1]` (`:3779`). So every committed position but the last is
provably a drafted token; only the final one can be an EOS that was never drafted, and that one already
lands last. Cropping the draft at its first EOS therefore makes an EOS-before-the-end impossible. When the
whole cropped draft is accepted, the guard at `:3777` drops the bonus token and leaves EOS last;
`_speculative_sampling` has the equivalent guard, so sampling is covered too.

Both crops fire on `generation_config._eos_token_tensor`, the same tensor `EosTokenCriteria` is built from
(`utils.py:1383-1384`), so a block can never be shortened for a token that would not have stopped
generation. MTP crops the returned block rather than breaking its drafting loop early, because the cache
correction crops a fixed `-num_mtp_layers` and a short block would desync it.

MTP also only reaches the bug with more than one layer — with one, the drafted EOS is already last and the
existing guard covers it. DeepSeek-V3/V3.1 and GLM-4.5/4.5-Air/4.6 ship one layer and are unaffected;
Inkling ships eight.

## The third commit

Main moved while these were open: #47877 reads `.weight.device` on the output embeddings and #48007 drops
the anchor position before the head, so the DFlash test stub needed a `.weight` and 1:1 row mapping.
Without it the merge with current main fails every DFlash crop test, even though both branches are green on
their own.

## Verified on the real model

`meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` + `-assistant`, bf16 on one A100 80GB, greedy, `max_new_tokens=512`,
`block_size=16`. Same machine and weights in both arms. "past EOS" counts tokens committed after the first
EOS:

| prompt | plain greedy | dflash before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `List the first eight prime numbers…` | 184 tok, EOS@183 | 191 tok, **+21 past EOS** | 170 tok, +0 |
| `Name the four cardinal directions…` | 222 tok, EOS@221 | 296 tok, **+74 past EOS** | 222 tok, +0 |
| `Reply with exactly the word: done` | 94 tok, EOS@93 | 396 tok, **+302 past EOS** | 94 tok, +0 |
| `Count from 1 to 5…` | 255 tok, EOS@254 | 211 tok, **+15 past EOS** | 196 tok, +0 |
| `What is 2+2? Answer with just the number.` | 90 tok, EOS@89 | 494 tok, **+404 past EOS** | 90 tok, +0 |
| `List three primary colours…` | 374 tok, EOS@373 | 367 tok, +0 | 367 tok, +0 |

Caveat from the original PR: dflash is not token-for-token identical to plain greedy here, and was not
before this change either — block vs single-token verification uses different bf16 kernel shapes. The MTP
half is measured on a tiny random `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`, since I have no MTP checkpoint I can run
(Inkling-Small is 532 GB).

Tests: one class per generator in `test_candidate_generator.py` — first EOS, a repeated EOS (only a repeat
distinguishes "first" from "last"), a leading EOS, and the untouched cases. Both assert the logits are
cropped alongside the tokens.

---

*AI-assisted contribution, per CONTRIBUTING.md: the patches, tests and measurements were drafted with
Claude Code, and the numbers above are from actual local runs. The changed lines and the behaviour have
been reviewed by me before submitting.*

title: Add support for Lumma Model
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47929)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47929)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## PR Overview

This PR adds native support for the Lumma AI model to the transformers library, allowing users to load and run Lumma through the standard `from_pretrained(...)` API without requiring custom remote code.

Lumma by FrontiersMind is a Llama-style decoder with efficiency-oriented architectural choices - factorized embeddings, GQA, optional layer sharing, shared KV attention, and configurable Q/QK normalization.

### Architecture
  - Factorized embeddings to reduce the size of the embedding layers.
  - Grouped Query Attention (GQA) for more efficient attention.
  - Shared KV attention, where the value projection is reused from the key projection.
  - Q-norm / QK-norm support for normalizing queries and keys.
  - Optional layer sharing, allowing the same layers to be reused multiple times.
  - RoPE and Llama-style MLP, keeping the familiar Llama architecture.

I would really appreciate it if you could take a look at this PR and share any feedback or suggestions. We’re hoping to get this merged soon, so please let me know if there’s anything that needs to be addressed before merging. We’ll be happy to make the necessary changes promptly.

title: Continuous batching auto-switches to flash_attention_3 on unsupported GPUs (Turing/T4), crashing — regression from 5.14.1
body:
### System Info

- Affected: `transformers==5.15.0` (also current `main` / `5.16.0.dev0`). **Not** reproduced on the `v5.14.1` release.
- Same environment also moved `kernels==0.15.2` → `kernels==0.16.0`, and the `kernels-community/vllm-flash-attn3` Hub kernel is now pulled.
- GPU: NVIDIA **T4** (Turing, SM 7.5), i.e. **pre-Ampere**. `flash_attn` is not pip-installed (only `transformers[kernels]`).
- Container: `pytorch/pytorch:2.8.0-cuda12.8-cudnn9-devel`.

### Who can help?

cc @remi-or @IlyasMoutawwakil (continuous batching)

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

Running generation with continuous batching (`generate_batch` / `use_transformers_continuous_batching=True`) on a **pre-Ampere** GPU (NVIDIA T4).

On `5.15.0`, continuous batching auto-switches the attention implementation from `sdpa` to `flash_attention_3` and loads the `kernels-community/vllm-flash-attn3` Hub kernel:

```
ContinuousBatchingLogger - WARNING - Continuous batching is much better when using flash attention. Switching from sdpa to flash_attention_3. If you need to use eager or sdpa, use paged|eager or paged|sdpa as the `attn_implementation`.
transformers.modeling_utils - WARNING - You do not have `flash_attn` installed, using `paged|kernels-community/vllm-flash-attn3` from the `kernels` library instead!
```

The generation loop then crashes, because that kernel requires newer hardware:

```
ContinuousBatchingLogger - ERROR - Error in generation loop: mha_fwd, /build/source/flash-attn/flash_api_stable.cpp:716, FlashAttention only supports Ampere GPUs or newer.
ContinuousBatchingLogger - ERROR - Generation thread terminated unexpectedly.
ContinuousBatchingLogger - ERROR - Requests ['req_0', 'req_1', 'req_2'] not found in results.
```

Because the generation thread dies, no completions are returned, which then breaks downstream code that assumes at least one completion.

The same code runs fine on `v5.14.1` (with `kernels==0.15.2`): continuous batching does **not** switch to `flash_attention_3`, and generation completes normally.

Observed in CI on a single-GPU T4 runner (downstream project TRL):
- Passing: `transformers==5.14.1` / `kernels==0.15.2` — https://github.com/huggingface/trl/actions/runs/31371150907/job/93400203818
- Failing: `transformers==5.15.0` / `kernels==0.16.0` — https://github.com/huggingface/trl/actions/runs/31582787840/job/94069521759

Workaround: pass `attn_implementation="paged|sdpa"` (or `paged|eager`).

### Expected behavior

Continuous batching should not switch to `flash_attention_3` on GPUs that cannot run it. The auto-switch should be gated on device capability (or fall back to `sdpa`) instead of hard-crashing the generation thread, as was the case on `v5.14.1`.

> Note: I don't yet have a minimal non-CI reproduction on non-Ampere hardware; the above is from CI logs plus a version bisect (`model_runner.py` is byte-identical between `v5.14.1` and `v5.15.0`, so the change is in the attention/kernel default selection). I'll add the exact regressing change — and whether it originates in `transformers` or in the `kernels` default resolution — as a follow-up once pinned.

title: Keep MXFP4 weights quantized on XPU when use_kernels is set
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47923)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47923)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Summary

`Mxfp4HfQuantizer` dequantizes to bf16 whenever `use_kernels` is set on any
accelerator other than CPU, because kernel layers were assumed to need dense
weights. That no longer holds on XPU: the `megablocks` layer already mapped to
XPU for `MegaBlocksMoeMLP` reads MXFP4 experts natively. This adds `xpu` to the
same allow-list CPU is already on.

## Why

Dequantizing inflates the expert weights ~3.8x, and every MoE forward then
re-reads that inflated tensor on a path that is already bandwidth-bound.

Measured on GPT-OSS with Intel Arc Pro B60, `torch 2.13.0+xpu`: quantized, the
model fits on a single card; dequantized, it has to be spread across several,
and is still slower end to end. Generated output is unchanged.

## Dependencies

Requires the `megablocks` change that teaches the XPU layer to read the triton
MXFP4 representation, and a `megablocks` build carrying it published on the Hub.
Until then the XPU layer would receive weights it cannot interpret.

title: Fix CLIP _init_weights when a child module carries quantized weights
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47921)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47921)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #47920

`CLIPPreTrainedModel._init_weights` initializes the parameters of **child** modules by name —
`module.q_proj.weight`, `module.fc1.weight`, `module.text_projection.weight`, and so on. A quantized
checkpoint replaces `weight` on those children with packed tensors (`weight_packed` for
compressed-tensors, `qweight` for GPTQ/AWQ), so loading one raises

```
AttributeError: 'Linear' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

from the initialization pass that runs at the end of loading: `_finalize_model_loading` →
`_initialize_missing_keys` → `initialize_weights` → `smart_apply` → `_init_weights`
(`modeling_utils.py:4517`, `:2476-2491`). For a packed format the packed layout is installed **before**
the weights are loaded, by `transformers` itself —
`CompressedTensorsHfQuantizer._process_model_before_weight_loading` calls
`self.compressor.compress_model(model)` (`quantizers/quantizer_compressed_tensors.py:117-121`).

A container such as `CLIPAttention` owns no parameter of its own, so `_initialize_weights`' skip
conditions never apply to it for a class living in `transformers.*`, and it always reaches
`_init_weights`.

This PR routes every child-weight initialization in `CLIPPreTrainedModel._init_weights` through a
small helper that skips a child with no `weight`, which is the guard the generic
`PreTrainedModel._init_weights` already applies to `nn.Linear`/`nn.Conv*` (`modeling_utils.py:2392`)
and to the norms (`:2418-2421`, *"Norms can exist without weights"*). It is the same shape as the
merged #38013, which fixed this class of failure in `modeling_qwen2_5_omni.py` for AutoAWQ
checkpoints.

`MetaClip2PreTrainedModel` inherits this method through modular and the converter inlines the body,
so `models/metaclip_2/modeling_metaclip_2.py` is regenerated in the same commit
(`python utils/modular_model_converter.py --files_to_parse src/transformers/models/metaclip_2/modular_metaclip_2.py`);
MetaCLIP-2 gets the fix with it.

Initialization of a non-quantized model is unchanged: the seeded `state_dict` of a tiny `CLIPModel`
hashes to the same SHA-256 before and after the patch (`a6808d27…`). The change also removes a
pre-existing crash for `CLIPForImageClassification` with `num_labels == 0`, where `classifier` is an
`nn.Identity`.

### Verification

```
# the new regression test
pytest tests/models/clip/test_modeling_clip.py -k init_weights_with_quantized
  -> 1 passed          (with the patch)
  -> 1 failed, AttributeError: 'Linear' object has no attribute 'weight'   (with the patch reverted)

# the test files utils/tests_fetcher.py selects for this diff
pytest tests/models/clip/test_modeling_clip.py tests/models/metaclip_2/test_modeling_metaclip_2.py \
       tests/models/sam3/test_modeling_sam3.py tests/models/sam3_video/test_modeling_sam3_video.py \
       tests/models/vision_text_dual_encoder/test_modeling_vision_text_dual_encoder.py
  -> 869 passed, 960 skipped, 6 xfailed, 8 failed in 6m18s

# repo checks
python utils/checkers.py ruff_check, ruff_format, init_isort, sort_auto_mappings, modeling_structure
  -> all OK (ruff over the whole tree)
python utils/checkers.py <all REPO_CONSISTENCY_CHECKERS>
  -> All 17 checks passed
```

The 8 failures are all `test_multi_gpu_data_parallel_forward` (4 in the CLIP file, 4 in the MetaCLIP-2
file). They are pre-existing on this machine: the same 8 fail on the parent commit, and nothing else in
those five files fails.

The `types` checker fails identically on the parent commit with the `ty` version I have installed, so
it is not affected by this diff.

### Scope

The same pattern — `_init_weights` dereferencing a child module's `.weight`/`.bias` — is present in 83
of 488 `modeling_*.py` files on `main`, and I measured the identical `AttributeError` for `T5`,
`Mamba2`, `LLaVA` (CLIP vision tower) and `Gemma3` (SigLIP vision tower). The issue linked above has
the full analysis, including why marking the quantized modules `_is_hf_initialized` (as the
bitsandbytes/torchao/quanto/mxfp4/sinq integrations do) does not fix it, and why the 4.x
"skip a fully loaded subtree" rule does not either. I kept this PR to CLIP; happy to extend the guard
to the other families in whatever batching you prefer.

Not applicable — I am not a first-time contributor (#46277, #47940). Per the *Agentic contributions*

title: _init_weights crashes on quantized checkpoints for models that initialize child modules by name
body:
### System Info

```
- `transformers` version: 5.16.0.dev0 (source, main @ dfb1af66d4) and 5.15.0 (wheel)
                          the relevant code is byte-identical in both
- Platform: Linux-6.5.0-35-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
- Python version: 3.11.12
- Huggingface_hub version: 1.6.0
- Safetensors version: 0.8.0
- Accelerate version: 1.12.0
- compressed-tensors version: 0.15.0.1
- PyTorch version (GPU?): 2.10.0+cu128 (True, RTX 4090)
```

Also reproduced against `transformers` 4.51.3 to establish the v4 -> v5 behaviour change (see below).

### Who can help?

@CyrilVallez (model loading / weight initialization), @molbap (vision models)

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [X] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [X] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

`CLIPPreTrainedModel._init_weights` initializes the parameters of **child** modules by name
(`models/clip/modeling_clip.py:417-428` for the attention/MLP projections, `:429-452` for the
contrastive projections and the classifier):

```python
elif isinstance(module, CLIPAttention):
    init.normal_(module.q_proj.weight, std=in_proj_std)   # not `module`'s own parameter
```

A quantized checkpoint replaces `weight` on those children with packed tensors — `weight_packed`
for compressed-tensors, `qweight` for GPTQ/AWQ — so that read raises. The script below puts a model
into exactly that state and then runs the initialization pass that `from_pretrained` runs at the end
of loading, so it needs no quantization library:

```python
import torch
from torch import nn
from transformers import CLIPConfig, CLIPModel
from transformers.models.clip.modeling_clip import CLIPAttention, CLIPMLP

config = CLIPConfig(
    text_config={"hidden_size": 32, "intermediate_size": 37, "num_hidden_layers": 2,
                 "num_attention_heads": 4, "vocab_size": 99, "max_position_embeddings": 64},
    vision_config={"hidden_size": 32, "intermediate_size": 37, "num_hidden_layers": 2,
                   "num_attention_heads": 4, "image_size": 30, "patch_size": 2},
    projection_dim=16,
)
model = CLIPModel(config)

# What a packed checkpoint leaves on a quantized Linear: no `weight`, packed tensors instead.
for module in model.modules():
    if isinstance(module, (CLIPAttention, CLIPMLP)):
        for child in module.children():
            if isinstance(child, nn.Linear):
                out_features, in_features = child.weight.shape
                del child._parameters["weight"]
                child.register_parameter("weight_packed", nn.Parameter(
                    torch.zeros(out_features, in_features // 8, dtype=torch.int32), requires_grad=False))

# Everything the checkpoint provides is flagged as loaded, as the loader does.
for param in model.parameters():
    param._is_hf_initialized = True
for module in model.modules():
    if hasattr(module, "_is_hf_initialized"):
        del module._is_hf_initialized

model._initialize_missing_keys(is_quantized=True)
```

```
AttributeError: 'Linear' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

The same script crashes with `T5ForConditionalGeneration`, `Mamba2ForCausalLM`,
`LlavaForConditionalGeneration` and `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration` (packing the vision tower) once
the module classes in the filter are swapped — 5 families measured, all on `main`.

The state is not artificial: for a packed format, `CompressedTensorsHfQuantizer._process_model_before_weight_loading`
calls `self.compressor.compress_model(model)` **before** the weights are loaded
(`quantizers/quantizer_compressed_tensors.py:117-121`), and `_finalize_model_loading` then runs
`_initialize_missing_keys` → `initialize_weights` → `_init_weights` over the whole tree
(`modeling_utils.py:4517`).

### Expected behavior

Loading a quantized checkpoint should not raise. Initialization only needs to seed the keys the
checkpoint does not provide, and every value in a fully quantized checkpoint comes from the file.

### Root cause

`_initialize_weights` skips a module only if (`modeling_utils.py:2438-2461`):

1. `module._is_hf_initialized` is set, or
2. `is_custom_code` **and** every **direct** (`recurse=False`) parameter/buffer is flagged.

A container such as `CLIPAttention` owns no parameter of its own, so under `is_custom_code=False` —
i.e. for every class living in `transformers.*` — it always reaches `_init_weights`, which then reads
its children's `weight`.

`transformers` 4.51.3 did not do this. `set_initialized_submodules` (`modeling_utils.py:584-598`)
marked a module `_is_hf_initialized` when its **recursive** `state_dict()` keys were all present in
the checkpoint, which is vacuously satisfied for a container whose children are all loaded. Measured,
same scenario as above:

| | 4.51.3 | 5.15.0 / main |
|---|---|---|
| CLIP, 24 packed Linears | parents 8/8 marked initialized → **no error** | **AttributeError** |
| T5, 32 packed Linears | parents 10/10 marked initialized → **no error** | **AttributeError** |

### Scope

An AST scan of `main` finds **83 of 488** `modeling_*.py` files whose `_init_weights` dereferences a
child module's `.weight`/`.bias`, including `siglip`, `siglip2`, `t5` (+ `mt5`, `umt5`, `longt5`,
`switch_transformers`, `udop`, `pix2struct`, `t5gemma`), `mamba`, `mamba2`, `falcon_mamba`,
`recurrent_gemma`, `kosmos2`, `phi4_multimodal`, `git`, `clvp`, `groupvit`, `owlvit`, `owlv2`,
`altclip`, `chinese_clip`, `clipseg`, `x_clip`, `align`, `detr`, `conditional_detr`, `maskformer`,
`oneformer`, and the MoE routers of `qwen3_next` / `qwen3_5_moe` / `qwen3_omni_moe`. Whether a given
family crashes depends only on whether the dereferenced child is among the quantized modules.

None of this duplication is linked by `# Copied from`, so `check_copies` neither propagates a fix nor
flags the divergence.

For a real-world profile: the public checkpoint `simaai/Gemma3-SigLIP448-GPTQ-Safetensors` is
compressed-tensors `pack-quantized` with an empty `ignore` list and `config_groups` that name
`model.vision_tower.encoder.layers.*.self_attn.{q,k,v,out}_proj` and `.mlp.{fc1,fc2}` explicitly —
the module set whose packing I measured to crash `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration`. I did not download
that checkpoint, so I am reporting the config match, not a load I ran.

### Two alternatives that do not work

Both were measured, in case they come up:

- **Marking the quantized modules `_is_hf_initialized`**, which `integrations/bitsandbytes.py`,
  `torchao.py`, `quanto.py`, `mxfp4.py` and `sinq.py` all do, does not help: the flag stops
  `_initialize_weights` from visiting that child, but the parent's `_init_weights` branch reaches into
  it by name anyway. Same `AttributeError` with and without the flag.
- **Restoring the v4 "skip a fully loaded subtree" rule** does not fix CLIP.
  `_move_missing_keys_from_meta_to_device` re-creates every non-persistent buffer with
  `torch.empty_like` (`modeling_utils.py:4768-4772`) and `_load_parameter_into_model` (`:518-525`)
  does not flag them, so a module with a non-persistent buffer anywhere in its subtree can never be
  skipped. CLIP has two (`position_ids` in `CLIPTextEmbeddings` / `CLIPVisionEmbeddings`), so
  simulating that rule on a fully loaded `CLIPModel` still runs `_init_weights` on the root, on both
  towers and on both embedding modules (5 modules out of 66 for a tiny config), which moves the
  `AttributeError` from `CLIPAttention` to the `CLIPModel` branch (`module.text_projection.weight` —
  a plain `nn.Linear`, and packed by any `Linear`-targeting scheme) rather than removing it. It does
  fully cover T5 (0/103 modules run) and Mamba2 (0/22), but a decoder-only model keeps rotary
  non-persistent buffers, so the root branch always runs there too (Llama: 3/33). A per-branch guard
  in the model file is the only thing that holds regardless.

### Proposed fix

The guard the generic `PreTrainedModel._init_weights` already applies to `nn.Linear`/`nn.Conv*`
(`modeling_utils.py:2392`) and to the norms (`:2418-2421`, "Norms can exist without weights"), applied
to the child dereferences as well. This is the shape of the merged #38013, which fixed the same class
of failure in `modeling_qwen2_5_omni.py` for AutoAWQ checkpoints.

PR #47921 does that for CLIP (and MetaCLIP-2, which inlines the method through modular). Two smaller
pieces are left for follow-ups, unless you would rather see them folded in:

- the `nn.Embedding` branch of the generic `_init_weights` (`modeling_utils.py:2402-2406`) is the one
  branch there that is still unguarded, so a checkpoint with quantized embeddings raises
  `AttributeError: 'Embedding' object has no attribute 'weight'` even with the CLIP fix applied;
- `modeling_clip.py:172`, `:208` and `:239` read `position_embedding.weight` / `patch_embedding.weight`
  in `forward`, so for a packed embedding or patch embedding the fix above moves the failure from load
  time to first forward rather than removing it.

Happy to extend the same guard to the rest of the 83 families in whatever batching you prefer.

### Disclosure

This report was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). Every number, line reference and failure
above was produced by running the code against the installed packages. The reproduction script is
inlined above; the variants for the other families differ only in the model class and the module
filter. I am the author of the analysis and the patch, and I ran the verification myself.

title: Fix/bitsandbytes caching allocator warmup
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47919)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47919)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

Fixes #47914 
caching_allocator_warmup crashes with AttributeError when loading a bitsandbytes-quantized model with a PEFT adapter (or any scenario where _load_pretrained_model runs after the model has been quantized).

Main changes:
* Renamed is_hqq_or_quark → is_quant_method_with_non_standard_params to reflect the broader purpose
* Added QuantizationMethod.BITS_AND_BYTES to the exemption set

Because:
bitsandbytes' Int8Params stores its internal quantization tensors (SCB, CB) as plain Python attributes, not via register_parameter() or register_buffer(). When expand_device_map produces entries like layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.base_layer.SCB, the warmup path calls get_parameter_or_buffer() on them and fails and crashes: AttributeError: 'layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.base_layer.SCB' is neither a parameter, buffer, nor extra state. caching_allocator_warmup already skips the warmup entirely for HQQ and Quark, precisely because those quantization methods also keep internal tensors outside the canonical PyTorch parameter/buffer registries. The BITS_AND_BYTES method is missing from that exemption list, so we need to add it up.

title: Moving mlinter to 0.1.4
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47918)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47918)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Bumps `transformers-mlinter` to [`0.1.4`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers-mlinter) to pick up the new rules (TRF020 to TRF057), and resolves everything those rules flag.

The base pinned `transformers-mlinter==0.1.2`, whose `utils/rules.toml` carried only TRF001–TRF019. This bump adds **37 new rules in the TRF020–TRF057 range**, and every finding they reported across the repo is resolved: `make check-code-quality` passes with 0 modeling structure violations.

No pre-existing rule changes behavior: the TRF001–TRF019 rule definitions and allowlists are exactly the base's, with justification comments added on top. In particular **TRF018 is untouched** — it is an old rule and the base already allowlists the 16 models that would otherwise trip it.

## Cherry-picked from other PRs

To avoid duplicating work already done elsewhere. Both are cherry-picked with `-x`, preserving original authorship:

- **#47866** (@zucchini-nlp), `5b09535` — renames 9 test files from `test_processor_*.py` to `test_processing_*.py` (`auto`, `glm46v`, `glm4v`, `glm_image`, `kosmos2_5`, `lighton_ocr`, `ovis2`, `sam2`, `sam2_video`). Those tests were never missing, just named where `TRF038` does not look for them. Clears 5 of the 7 `TRF038` findings.
- **#47768** (@guarin), `1ed5317` — adds the missing `@auto_docstring` decorators that **TRF057 is the rule for** (authored alongside it in mlinter PR #21). Without it TRF057 is red across many models; with it, only 4 findings remain, all in models added after that PR was written, fixed below.
- **#47536** — nothing to take. That PR introduces the `TRF020` rule definition and bumps the pin; it contains no model-side fix, and it carries the same `axk2` finding this PR started with. The rule itself already arrives here via mlinter main, so the only open question was the `axk2` finding, handled under *Allow lists* below.

### Conflict resolution worth reviewing

#47768 conflicted in 8 places on the four `Inkling` config classes. The two sides were complementary rather than competing:

- #47768 (Aug 4) enabled `@auto_docstring` and documented ~150 lines of config fields
- `main` (Aug 11, #47902) had `@auto_docstring(checkpoint="thinkingmachines/Inkling")` **commented out** behind a TODO: *"uncomment once all fields below are documented"*

Since #47768 documents exactly those fields, the TODO is discharged. Resolved by enabling the decorator **and** keeping `main`'s newer `checkpoint=` argument (plus `custom_intro` on `InklingConfig`). `utils/check_docstrings.py` reports no Inkling errors, so this is verified rather than assumed.

## Fixes

| rule | model | change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TRF029` | axk2 | `AXK2GatedRMSNorm.__init__` no longer takes `eps` alongside `config`; it reads `config.rms_norm_eps` internally. Both call sites were already passing exactly that value. |
| `TRF043` | cohere_compass | Dropped the unused `position_ids` parameter from `CohereCompassAttention.forward`; it flows through `**kwargs` so padding-free flash-attention can consume it. No caller was passing it. |
| `TRF055` | qwen3_omni_moe | `Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerTextPreTrainedModel.config` is now an annotation rather than an assignment, which was shadowing `config_class` resolution. This was the only assignment form left in the repo. |
| `TRF038` | cohere_compass | Added `test_image_processing_cohere_compass.py` and `test_video_processing_cohere_compass.py`, mirroring the qwen2_vl / qwen3_vl tests that these `pass`-subclass processors inherit from. |
| `TRF057` | cohere_compass, muse_glimmer, muse_glimmer_assistant | Added the 4 missing `@auto_docstring` decorators (see below). |

### TRF057 — missing `@auto_docstring`

These 4 are the ones #47768 could not have covered, since all three models were added after it was written. `@auto_docstring` goes **innermost** on methods, as the rule requires:

| target | file |
| --- | --- |
| `CohereCompassVisionModel` | `modular_cohere_compass.py` |
| `MuseGlimmerVisionModel` | `modular_muse_glimmer.py` |
| `MuseGlimmerVisionModel.forward` | `modular_muse_glimmer.py` |
| `MuseGlimmerAssistantModel.forward` | `modular_muse_glimmer_assistant.py` |

`TRF056` (no `.item()` / `.tolist()` in `forward`) reported nothing.

### Docstring fallout from the cherry-pick

#47768 also touches `utils/auto_docstring.py`, and together with the new decorators that surfaced three `check_docstrings` failures in models newer than it. Fixed at the **modular** source, since fixing the generated files would be reverted on the next conversion:

- Redundant `video_grid_thw` / `image_grid_thw` arg docs, now supplied centrally — removed from `modular_kimi_k25.py` and `modular_hunyuan_vl.py`. `muse_glimmer` inherits `get_video_features` from `Kimi_K25Model`, so the kimi_k25 fix covers it too.
- `MuseGlimmerVisionModel.forward` needed `grid_thw` documented once decorated.

## Allow lists — justified in place

Per @ArthurZucker's review: every non-empty allowlist now carries a comment in `utils/rules.toml` saying what is on it and why, so the exemption is readable next to the rule instead of living in a PR thread. Each entry was re-checked against a run with all allowlists emptied (228 findings), so the counts and the model lists in those comments are measured, not estimated. Two entries no longer fire at all and were dropped: `sam2` (TRF038) and `mimo_v2_flash` (TRF041).

Short version of what the comments say:

| rule | why the list exists |
| --- | --- |
| `TRF020`, `TRF034` | Mostly false positives: the rule resolves a class's base chain only inside the linted file, so `modular_*.py` inheritance from another model reads as a missing base while the generated `modeling_*.py` is compliant — checked class by class (13 models for TRF034, `axk2` for TRF020). Upstream: mlinter#27. TRF034 also has 5 real ones (`dinov3_convnext`, `openai`, `tipsv2_dpt`, `x_clip`'s `PromptGeneratorLayer`, `xcodec2`'s `Xcodec2ResNetBlock`), left for a follow-up. |
| `TRF035` | 4 `# noqa`s that ruff needs: one deliberate re-export (`hunyuan_vl`) and three modular-converter artifacts (`step3p7` F401 import that picks Qwen2-VL's 2-axis vision RoPE, `nemotron3_5_asr` quoted forward reference, `zaya` `del` of an inherited name). Deleting the suppression just moves the failure to ruff, so the fix belongs upstream. |
| `TRF038` | Verified by @molbap: only `nougat` and `glmga` genuinely have no test. The rest are tested models whose processor / feature extractor has no dedicated test file, and the rule pairs each source file with its own test. Per @zucchini-nlp, enforce for new models and backfill the old families later. |
| `TRF041` | 35 branches over 13 models (openai alone has 11). Each `# CODEPATH:` note has to name the checkpoints that take each path — only the model owner knows that, and guessing would be worse than the missing note. Follow-up per model. |
| `TRF016`, `TRF019` | Inherited unchanged from the base pin; the live entries need a decision from the flag / checkpoint owner (`do_convert_rgb` that no `_preprocess` reads; `_defaults` that has to move to `processor_config.json` on the Hub first). |
| `TRF018` | 15 of the 16 spell the base call `PreTrainedModel._init_weights(module)` instead of `super()._init_weights(module)` — the form a modular file needs, since `super()` there resolves to the inherited model. 459 files use the spelling the rule accepts, these 15 the other. `radio` is the one real case. |
| `TRF043`, `TRF046`, `TRF051`, `TRF053` | These four have no `cutoff_date`, so they fire across the pre-existing corpus (21 / 26 / 10 / 37 findings). Each fix is a per-model breaking change or behavior change — a public `forward` signature, a stateful module, an attention-dispatch branch, a loss path — so they go out one model per PR. For `TRF043` in particular, a `cutoff_date` upstream would express the legacy half better than a 21-model list. |

Fixing the models on these lists is explicitly **not** in this PR; it is the follow-up series agreed above.

## Review follow-ups on `step3p7`

- The three `# CODEPATH:` notes were cut to two lines each (@ArthurZucker: *"comment can be a lot shorter"*).
- `Step3p7DecoderLayer` no longer builds the MLP through a conditional expression: now that `Step3p7SparseMoeBlock` and `Step3p7MLP` share the `(config, layer_idx)` signature, it picks the class and calls it once. `tests/models/step3p7` passes (189 tests).

## Suppressed in place

**`TRF026`** on `MuseGlimmerTextNormedEmbedding` (`# trf-ignore: TRF026`) — also a false positive. The class is an `nn.Embedding` subclass and its forward does the embedding lookup through `super().forward()` before applying the norm, so it is not a pass-through wrapper and there is no inner module to hoist out.

## Linter blind spots found

8 findings were false positives, and 7 of those share one root cause: the rules resolve a class's base chain only within the file being linted, so normal `modular_*.py` inheritance from another model reads as a missing base. Filed as **huggingface/transformers-mlinter#27** with the evidence for `TRF034`, `TRF020` and `TRF026`, plus a note that `TRF018` accepts only one of the two spellings of the modular `_init_weights` sentinel in use here (459 files vs 15).

The 6 allowlist entries added for `TRF034` and `TRF020` should be removable once that issue is fixed — they record a deviation that does not actually exist.

## Testing

- `make fix-repo` clean, `make check-code-quality` passes (0 modeling structure violations, `ty` clean)
- `cohere_compass`, `muse_glimmer`, `axk2` and `qwen3_omni_moe` suites pass locally, including the two new cohere_compass processor test files

### System Info

### Describe the bug

Loading a model with a `TimmWrapperModel` sub-backbone (e.g., `facebook/Perception-LM-1B`) with `attn_implementation="sdpa"` fails:

```
ValueError: TimmWrapperModel does not support an attention implementation through
torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention yet.
```

`TimmWrapperPreTrainedModel` inherits `_supports_sdpa = False` from `PreTrainedModel`, so `_sdpa_can_dispatch()` raises. But timm models **already use SDPA internally** via `use_fused_attn()` — completely independent of transformers' dispatch. 

### Evidence 

1. **timm uses SDPA internally** — `timm/layers/attention.py`: `self.fused_attn = use_fused_attn()` → calls `F.scaled_dot_product_attention`
2. **TimmWrapper delegates to timm** — modeling_timm_wrapper.py forward: `self.timm_model.forward_features(pixel_values, **kwargs)`, no `attn_implementation` passed

title: Fix BltConfig missing decoder alias for get_text_config(decoder=True)
body:

`BltConfig` stores its decoder sub-config under `decoder_config`, but `Cache._prepare_cache_for_generation()` relies on
`PreTrainedConfig.get_text_config(decoder=True)`, which looks for a sub-config exposed under standard attribute names (e.g. `decoder`). Since `BltConfig` did not expose one, it fell back to the top-level `BltConfig`, which has no `num_hidden_layers`, causing:

Add a decoder property aliasing `decoder_config` so the generic cache initialization path works for Blt models.

title: this is an incorrect pr, plz ignore
body:
Fixes #47914 
`caching_allocator_warmup` crashes with `AttributeError` when loading a bitsandbytes-quantized model with a PEFT adapter (or any scenario where `_load_pretrained_model` runs after the model has been quantized).

Main changes:
* Renamed is_hqq_or_quark → is_quant_method_with_non_standard_params to reflect the broader purpose
* Added QuantizationMethod.BITS_AND_BYTES to the exemption set

Because:
bitsandbytes' `Int8Params` stores its internal quantization tensors (SCB, CB) as plain Python attributes, not via register_parameter() or register_buffer(). When expand_device_map produces entries like layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.base_layer.SCB, the warmup path calls get_parameter_or_buffer() on them and fails and crashes: AttributeError: 'layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.base_layer.SCB' is neither a parameter, buffer, nor extra state. caching_allocator_warmup already skips the warmup entirely for HQQ and Quark, precisely because those quantization methods also keep internal tensors outside the canonical PyTorch parameter/buffer registries. The BITS_AND_BYTES method is missing from that exemption list, so we need to add it up.

@SunMarc @MekkCyber

from peft import PeftModel

base_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(

Traceback:
```
File "transformers/modeling_utils.py", line 4677, in caching_allocator_warmup
    total_byte_count = get_total_byte_count(model, accelerator_device_map, hf_quantizer)
File "transformers/modeling_utils.py", line 4634, in get_total_byte_count
    param = model.get_parameter_or_buffer(param_name)

```

A clear and concise description of what you would expect to happen:
Loading a PEFT adapter on top of a bitsandbytes-quantized model should succeed.

…or parallelism and reduces memory pressure during DFlash assisted decoding.

Main changes:

- Add selective hidden-state capture via `output_hidden_states_layers`, so DFlash only stores the main-model hidden states needed by the assistant instead of retaining all layers.
- Update `DFlashTokenCandidateGenerator` to request only the configured target layers and prepare the assistant context from those sparse hidden states.
- Support TP-sharded DFlash assistant context when the assistant encoder projection uses `rowwise` tensor parallelism, avoiding materializing the full concatenated context on every rank.
- Fix DFlash with MuseGlimmer TP by letting its normed embedding module expose an `apply_norm=False` path, so DFlash can obtain raw noise-token embeddings without bypassing TP-aware embedding dispatch.
- Add default tensor-parallel plans for MuseGlimmer text, vision, multimodal projection, LM head, and MuseGlimmer assistant modules.

These changes allow DFlash to work correctly with MuseGlimmer/MuseGlimmer assistant in TP setups while reducing unnecessary hidden-state memory usage.

With these changes, MuseGlimmer DFlash generation works on 2 x 32GB GPUs for both text-only and image+text inputs.

title: Assisted/speculative decoding generates past an EOS that is accepted mid-block
body:
# Assisted/speculative decoding generates past an EOS that is accepted mid-block

### System info

- `transformers` 5.15.0 (reproduced on the `v5.15.0` tag)
- `torch` 2.13.0 — the minimal repro is CPU-only
- Originally observed on `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` + `-assistant` (DFlash), A100 80GB, bf16

### Who can help?

@Cyrilvallez (generate). The DFlash generator came in with #47867.

## Description

`_assisted_decoding` commits `n_matches + 1` tokens per round. When an accepted
token in the middle of that block is an EOS, generation does not stop: the whole
block is appended (and streamed) first, and the stopping check afterwards only
looks at the last committed token. The result is output that continues past EOS
and does not match plain greedy.

It is position-dependent, which makes it look intermittent — an EOS that happens
to land on the target's bonus token stops correctly.

## Minimal reproduction (CPU, tiny random model, no drafter needed)

The bug needs the EOS to be *accepted*, i.e. the target's own argmax must be EOS
at that position. Instead of hunting for such a prompt, run greedy first and then
declare one of the tokens the model actually produced to be the EOS.

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from transformers.generation.candidate_generator import CandidateGenerator
import transformers.generation.utils as gu

NAME, BLOCK, EOS_OFFSET = "hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM", 8, 3
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(NAME).eval()
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(NAME)
ids = tok("Hello world", return_tensors="pt").input_ids
plen = ids.shape[1]

cont = model.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=BLOCK * 2, do_sample=False,
                      eos_token_id=-1, pad_token_id=0)[0, plen:].tolist()
EOS = cont[EOS_OFFSET]                      # a token the model really emits

class BlockStub(CandidateGenerator):        # proposes the model's own continuation
    requires_model_outputs = False
    def get_candidates(self, input_ids, **kw):
        n = input_ids.shape[1] - plen
        nxt = cont[n:n + BLOCK]
        if not nxt:
            return input_ids, None
        return torch.cat([input_ids, torch.tensor([nxt])], dim=-1), None
    def update_candidate_strategy(self, input_ids, scores, num_matches):
        pass

base = model.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=BLOCK * 2, do_sample=False,
                      eos_token_id=EOS, pad_token_id=0)
gu.GenerationMixin._get_candidate_generator = lambda self, **kw: BlockStub()
spec = model.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=BLOCK * 2, do_sample=False,
                      eos_token_id=EOS, pad_token_id=0, prompt_lookup_num_tokens=BLOCK)

print(base[0, plen:].tolist())   # [30016, 7356, 9023, 25068]                   <- stops at EOS
print(spec[0, plen:].tolist())   # [30016, 7356, 9023, 25068, 22665, ... ]      <- 12 tokens past EOS
```

Observed: plain greedy returns 4 tokens, assisted returns 16 — **12 tokens after
the EOS**.

### On a real model

`meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` + its DFlash drafter, greedy, `max_new_tokens=128`,
prompt `"List the first eight prime numbers, one per line, with no commentary."`:

| | length | EOS index | ends with EOS |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain greedy | 122 | 121 | yes |
| `speculation_type="dflash"` | **128** | 121 | **no** |

The first 122 tokens are identical; the speculative stream then emits
`<|start|>assistant to=self<|message|>We`. Instrumenting the candidate generator
to record `(proposed, num_matches)` per round and locating the EOS in its commit
round explains the intermittency:

- EOS at offset 6 of an 8-token commit (an **accepted proposal**) → ran 6 tokens past it.
- On another prompt, EOS at offset 1 of a 2-token commit (the **bonus** token) → stopped correctly.

## Expected behavior

Greedy assisted decoding should return the same token stream as plain greedy, and
stop at the first EOS. Instead it continues past an EOS that was accepted inside a
committed block, so the two disagree on both content and length.

## Cause

Two things compound, both in `_assisted_decoding`:

1. The committed block is appended and streamed before any stopping check:
   ```python
   input_ids = torch.cat((input_ids, valid_tokens), dim=-1)   # utils.py:3808
   if streamer is not None:
       streamer.put(valid_tokens.cpu())
   ```
2. The check that follows uses the default `new_token_length=1`:
   ```python
   unfinished_sequences = unfinished_sequences & ~stopping_criteria(input_ids, scores)  # utils.py:3859
   ```
   and `EosTokenCriteria` only inspects the last `new_token_length` tokens
   (`stopping_criteria.py:580`):
   ```python
   is_done = torch.isin(input_ids[:, -new_token_length:], self.eos_token_id).any(dim=-1)
   ```

The existing guard at `utils.py:3777` does not cover it: it fires only when the
*entire* candidate block was accepted (`n_matches == candidate_length`), and its
`is_done_candidate` (`utils.py:3696`) is itself computed at `new_token_length=1`.

Classic autoregressive drafters largely avoid this because the draft stops at EOS,
leaving it last. Block proposers (DFlash `block_size` 16, MTP) hit it routinely.

This failure mode is already known in-repo — `PromptLookupCandidateGenerator`
truncates its candidates at the first EOS for exactly this reason
(`candidate_generator.py:1129`):

```python
# remove remaining candidate ids if an "eos" token is found, otherwise the target model may
# accept eos and the rest as valid, thus not stopping generation after "eos"
```

`DFlashTokenCandidateGenerator` has no equivalent.

## Fix

Trim the committed block at the first EOS, mirroring what
`PromptLookupCandidateGenerator` already does to its drafts. That also leaves EOS
as the last token, so the existing criteria fire unchanged:

```python
eos_tensor = generation_config._eos_token_tensor
if eos_tensor is not None and valid_tokens.shape[1] > 1:
    eos_hits = torch.nonzero(torch.isin(valid_tokens[0], eos_tensor.to(valid_tokens.device)))
    if eos_hits.numel() > 0:
        valid_tokens = valid_tokens[:, : eos_hits[0].item() + 1]
        n_matches = valid_tokens.shape[1] - 1
```

placed just after the existing length-budget clamp, recomputing `n_matches` the way
that clamp already does so `number_of_tokens_to_crop` stays consistent.

Note the obvious one-liner — passing `new_token_length=n_matches + 1` to the
stopping criteria at `utils.py:3859`, as `generation_diffusion_gemma.py:1088` does
for its canvas — is **not sufficient on its own**. Measured on the repro above it
takes the output from 16 tokens to 9, but 5 post-EOS tokens remain: it ends the
loop without undoing the commit.

`min_new_tokens` is unaffected: the logits processors suppress EOS until the
minimum is reached, so the target never accepts one for the trim to find (verified
at `min_new_tokens=0` → 4 tokens and `=10` → 16).

## Verification

Branch is 61 added lines (11 source, 50 test) on top of `main` (`dfb1af6`).

```
pytest tests/generation/test_utils.py tests/generation/test_candidate_generator.py \
       tests/generation/test_stopping_criteria.py
# 115 passed, 21 skipped, 3 failed
```

The 3 failures (`test_default_max_length_warning`,
`test_inputs_embeds_warn_without_ids_for_token_based_logit_processors`,
`test_validate_stopping_criteria`) fail identically on clean `main` without this
change.

The new test is armed: reverting only `generation/utils.py` to `main` makes it fail
with `generation continued past an accepted EOS: [750, 297, 297, 860, 860, 860,
860, 860]`, and it passes with the fix. `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean
on both touched files.

---

*AI-assisted contribution, per CONTRIBUTING.md: the patch, the repro and the test
were drafted with Claude Code, and the results above are from actual local runs.
The changed lines and the behaviour have been reviewed by me before submitting.*

---

Would you like a PR for this? I have the fix and the regression test above ready on
a branch off `main` (`dfb1af6`) — happy to open it, or to leave it if you would
rather handle the stopping logic differently.

title: Update sliding window indexing in continuous batching
body:

# What does this PR do?

Fixes the retrieval of historical tokens in sliding window layers during paged attention decoding.

**The Bug:** In `SlidingAttentionCacheAllocator`, the starting index for reading from the rolling buffer was pointing to stale tokens from the beginning of the buffer (instead of skipping them) once generation exceeded the sliding window size. This caused sliding layers to attend to incorrect tokens within the window, and affected context memory.

**The Fix:**

- Updated `start_index` to align with the oldest valid token in the cache so that generation picks up active tokens correctly in cyclic order.
- Made this change flag driven with `--cb_enable_sliding_window_decode / enable_sliding_window_decode` to ensure backward compatibility.

## Code Agent Policy

The Transformers repo is currently being overwhelmed by a large number of PRs and issue comments written by
code agents. These often are low-quality, or fix extremely minor issues that occur rarely or never in practice.

title: Fix compressed-tensors loading for KV-cache-only quantized models
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47904)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47904)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes loading of KV-cache-only quantized models (e.g. `inference-optimization/tinysmokeqwen3-fp8-kv-only`) with the compressed-tensors quantizer.

## Problem

In `_process_model_before_weight_loading`, the early return `if not remaining_groups: return` was added to skip `apply_quantization_config` when all config groups were already handled by the FP8 kernel path. However, `apply_quantization_config` is also responsible for setting up KV-cache quantization observers and scales. For models that **only** have KV-cache quantization (no weight quantization groups), `remaining_groups` is empty and the early return skips KV-cache setup entirely, causing the model to load without any quantization applied.

## Fix

Remove the early return so that `apply_quantization_config` always runs. When `remaining_groups` is empty, it receives an empty `config_groups` dict — this is a no-op for weight quantization but still correctly processes KV-cache quantization config.

## Example

Loading `inference-optimization/tinysmokeqwen3-fp8-kv-only`:

**Before (broken):** `apply_quantization_config` is skipped, KV-cache quantization is not applied, and the model behaves as if unquantized.

**After (fixed):** `apply_quantization_config` runs, KV-cache quantization observers/scales are correctly initialized, and the model loads as expected.

## Follow-up

- Add a dedicated test for KV-cache-only model loading in the compressed-tensors test suite
- Refactor compressed-tensors tests to use modern models and more robust test metrics

title: Support per-layer cache configuration and attention-mask selection
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47901)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47901)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Updates cache construction and attention-mask selection to support models whose layers use different cache settings.

Previously, `DynamicCache` and `StaticCache` derived one set of initialization arguments from the top-level config and reused it for every layer. They now initialize each cache layer from its corresponding layer config, preserving per-layer `sliding_window`, `attention_chunk_size`, and `number_of_conv_states` values.

Cache and mask helpers also inferred cache metadata from a fixed layer, which could select a linear-attention layer or an unpopulated KV layer instead of one representing the requested attention pattern. When no explicit `layer_idx` is provided, they now select a representative KV layer: dynamic caches prefer a populated matching layer, while static caches use the first matching KV layer in their fixed layout.

title: Fix DynamicCache reconstruction during ExecuTorch export
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47900)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47900)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes incorrect cache-update graphs when exporting models with `DynamicCache` to ExecuTorch.

`torch.export` uses the registered pytree functions to flatten and reconstruct DynamicCache during export. The current pytree registration keeps populated key/value tensors, but loses each layer's type and window size. As a result, updated layers are rebuilt as regular `DynamicLayer`s.

For sliding and chunked attention, `torch.export` can then trace unbounded cache growth instead of the bounded update implemented by `DynamicSlidingWindowLayer`. The immediate logits may still match because the attention mask hides older states, but the cache keeps growing, wasting memory and computation and potentially exceeding ExecuTorch's planned shape or memory limits.

For example, with `sliding_window=4096`, the cache should retain only the latest 4095 past states. Before this change, the exported graph could retain the entire history.

## How it works

The pytree context now records each layer's type, sliding window size, and populated state. Reconstruction recreates the layers in their original positions before restoring their key/value tensors, so `torch.export` traces the correct cache updates.

`DynamicCache` can now be initialized with pre-created layers, allowing reconstruction to establish the fixed layout during initialization. Unsupported specialized cache-layer classes raise a clear error instead of being silently converted.

## Who can review?

@ArthurZucker
@Cyrilvallez

# What does this PR do?

TLDR:
Create embeddings in fp64 if device supports it. Create MPS embeddings in fp32. There is no benefit to init with fp64 on CPU and then move to MPS for inference as CPU/MPS inference differences outweigh the impact of f32/fp64 difference. title: fix(whisper): prevent NaN propagation in fbank feature extraction
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47894)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47894)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

## Summary

Fixes #47885 — NaN values in an audio waveform (e.g. from a faulty microphone, corrupted file, or pre-processing bug) propagate through `WhisperFeatureExtractor` and corrupt the **entire** output feature matrix, making downstream models produce garbage output silently.

### Root Cause

In both the NumPy and Torch extraction paths the dynamic-range floor is computed as:

```python
log_spec = np.maximum(log_spec, log_spec.max() - 8.0)   # numpy
log_spec = torch.maximum(log_spec, log_spec.max() - 8.0) # torch
```

`np.max` / `torch.max` on an array containing even a single `NaN` returns `NaN`. Subtracting `8.0` from `NaN` is still `NaN`, and `np.maximum(anything, NaN)` propagates `NaN` to every cell, turning the full 80 × 3000 matrix into `NaN`.

### Fix

| Path | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| NumPy | `log_spec.max()` | `np.nanmax(log_spec)` (falls back to `-8.0` if all-NaN) |
| Torch (batched) | `log_spec.max(dim=2)[0].max(dim=1)[0]` | `torch.nanmax(...)` + `nan_to_num` guard |
| Torch (unbatched) | `log_spec.max()` | `torch.nanmax(log_spec)` + `nan_to_num` guard |

`torch.nanmax` is guarded with `hasattr(torch, "nanmax")` for compatibility with PyTorch < 1.11, falling back gracefully.

No public API is changed. For valid (finite) inputs the output is bit-identical to the existing behaviour.

### Test

Added `test_nan_sample_propagation` to `tests/models/whisper/test_feature_extraction_whisper.py`:

```python
def test_nan_sample_propagation(self):
    feature_extractor = WhisperFeatureExtractor()
    audio = np.random.randn(16000).astype(np.float32) * 0.05
    audio[8000] = np.nan
    feats = feature_extractor(audio, sampling_rate=16000, return_tensors="np")["input_features"]
    # One NaN sample should not make the entire 80x3000 matrix NaN
    self.assertLess(np.isnan(feats).mean(), 1.0)
```

title: Fix NeMo conversion for Parakeet TDT checkpoints without a <pad> token (parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2)
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47891)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47891)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

`src/transformers/models/parakeet/convert_nemo_to_hf.py` fails on NVIDIA's `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2` checkpoint, which matters because v2 is distributed only as a `.nemo` file and this converter is the sole path to an HF-format checkpoint for it. The failure has two parts, and the second one is silent.

**Bug 1, a crash.** v2's NeMo vocab has 1024 labels and, unlike v3's, contains no `<pad>` entry. `convert_tdt_config` calls `labels.index("<pad>")` unconditionally and raises `ValueError: '<pad>' is not in list`.

**Bug 2, silent corruption.** If the crash is papered over by simply appending a `<pad>` token, the TDT branch of `write_processor` places `<pad>` at id 1024 and `<blank>` at id 1025. The checkpoint's joint head emits 1030 logits (1025 token logits plus 5 duration logits) and its blank id is 1024. Decoding with blank at 1025 produces transcripts that look plausible but are subtly wrong, and nothing errors. This is the dangerous case, since a user would ship it without noticing.

## The fix

When a TDT vocab carries no `<pad>` entry, take the existing RNN-T ordering: add `<blank>` first so it lands on `len(labels)`, which is exactly where the checkpoint's blank id points, and reuse the blank id as `pad_token_id`. v3 checkpoints, which do carry `<pad>`, are unaffected and keep the current TDT path. The change is two small hunks and introduces no new configuration surface.

## Verification

After this fix, we converted `nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2` and validated the result against the NeMo/PyTorch reference implementation. A hand-rolled greedy TDT loop over the converted model matches `generate()` token for token on a 30 second probe (82 of 82 tokens), and end-to-end transcripts remained token-exact across a multi-hour audiobook validation corpus. Without the second fix, the same pipeline yields plausible but wrong transcripts, which is how we found the bug in the first place.

Converted config facts for reviewers who want to spot-check: `vocab_size=1025`, `blank_token_id=1024`, `durations=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`, and the encoder is identical to v3's, so only the tokenizer and vocab handling differ between the two releases.

title: Fix ASR pipeline mono conversion for channels-last audio (fixes #47886)
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47888)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47888)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #47886.

`AutomaticSpeechRecognitionPipeline` averaged multi-channel input over a hardcoded
`axis=0`, which assumes channels-first `(channels, samples)`. `soundfile.read`,
`librosa.load(..., mono=False)` and `scipy.io.wavfile.read` all return channels-**last**
`(samples, channels)`, so on that layout the mean ran across *time*: a 3-second stereo
clip collapsed to 2 numbers, was padded back to 30s of silence, and transcribed as
`' you'`.

The pipeline logged a warning saying the conversion had happened. It had, along the
wrong axis.

```python
stereo, sr = sf.read(buf, dtype="float32")   # (48000, 2)
asr(mono)     # ' See you in the next video!'
asr(stereo)   # ' you'          <- before
asr(stereo)   # ' See you in the next video!'   <- after
```

## The fix

Infer the channel axis rather than assume it. Real audio has far more samples than
channels, so the shorter axis is the channel axis. `(2, N)` keeps working exactly as
before; `(N, 2)` stops being destroyed.

Also report `tuple(inputs.shape)` in the warning instead of `inputs.ndim`. The old
message interpolated `ndim`, so it printed "got 2" for every 2-D input regardless of
channel count, and the number that would actually help you debug never appeared.

## Why not raise instead

That is a reasonable alternative and I would switch if you prefer it. The two sibling
pipelines already reject multi-channel outright:

```python
# pipelines/audio_classification.py:232
if len(inputs.shape) != 1:
    raise ValueError("We expect a single channel audio input for AudioClassificationPipeline")

# pipelines/zero_shot_audio_classification.py:119
if len(audio.shape) != 1:
    raise ValueError("We expect a single channel audio input for ZeroShotAudioClassificationPipeline")
```

So the same stereo array raises a clear `ValueError` in two pipelines and silently
transcribes as `' you'` in the third. I kept the conversion because it is existing
documented behaviour and removing it would break callers who currently pass `(2, N)`
successfully, but making ASR raise like its siblings is a three-line change if that is
the preferred direction.

I left `ndim > 2` alone deliberately; that is a separate question from the reported bug.

## Tests

`test_multichannel_mono_conversion_is_layout_agnostic` covers `(N, 2)`, `(2, N)`, and
2-D mono in both orientations, asserting all four match the 1-D baseline.

It fails on `main` with `AssertionError: choose a window size 400 that is [2, 2]` from
torchaudio, which is the bug surfacing as a 2-sample waveform.

```
tests/pipelines/test_pipelines_automatic_speech_recognition.py
    before: 5 failed, 16 passed, 35 skipped
    after:  5 failed, 17 passed, 35 skipped
```

Identical failures before and after, all pre-existing in my environment
(`test_return_timestamps_ctc_fast`, `test_pipeline_generation_kwargs` and friends), so
no regressions introduced. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` both clean.

## Who can review?

@ylacombe @eustlb (audio pipelines)

title: fix(qwen3_5,qwen3_next): sample GatedDeltaNet A in float32 to avoid -…
body:
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:start -->
[![CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=47887)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=47887)
<!-- ci-dashboard-badge:end -->

# fix(qwen3_5,qwen3_next): sample GatedDeltaNet A in float32 to avoid -inf A_log under bf16

Under `bfloat16` `torch.empty(...).uniform_(0,16)` can round to `0.0` so `log(A)` becomes `-inf`, freezing that head's decay at `0`. Sample `A` in `float32` before `log` in `__init__` and `_init_weights` for `Qwen3_5`, `Qwen3_5-MoE` and `Qwen3-Next` (modeling + modular). Matches `Mamba2`.

Fixes #47831

# What does this PR do?

Fixes #47831

Under `bfloat16`, the GatedDeltaNet decay parameter `A_log` is initialized from `A = torch.empty(self.num_v_heads).uniform_(0,16)` which inherits the model's `dtype`. In `bfloat16` that `uniform_(0,16)` rounds to exactly `0.0` with ~0.4% probability per head. `torch.log(0) = -inf` so `A = exp(A_log) = 0` → `g = -A*softplus(a+dt_bias) = 0` (head never forgets) and `dg/dA_log = 0` (gradient frozen, can never recover). On the 35B-A3B hybrid config (32 value heads × 30 GDN layers ≈960 draws) this is reliably 3–6 dead heads at every initialization.

**Change:** Sample `A` in `float32` before `log`, matching the reference already used in `Mamba2Mixer` and `modeling_mamba2.py`:

- `__init__`: `torch.empty(self.num_v_heads, dtype=torch.float32).uniform_(0,16)` in `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet`, `Qwen3_5MoeGatedDeltaNet`, `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet` (modeling + modular)
- `_init_weights`: `torch.empty(module.num_v_heads, dtype=torch.float32, device=module.A_log.device).uniform_(0,16).log_()` in all 6 files (`modeling` + `modular` for `qwen3_5`, `qwen3_5_moe`, `qwen3_next`)

This keeps `A_log` finite for every head regardless of model `dtype`, under both construction and `_init_weights` re-initialization. Forward already uses `A_log.float().exp()`, so no behavior change beyond the init distribution's precision (which is intended).

**Dependencies:** None. **Docs:** N/A (init-only, no public API).

**Repro** (from issue, seed 0):

```python
import torch
torch.manual_seed(0)
num_v, layers = 32, 30
def count_dead(dtype, float32_fix=False):
    dead=0
    for _ in range(layers):
        A = torch.empty(num_v, dtype=torch.float32 if float32_fix else dtype).uniform_(0,16)
        dead += int((~torch.isfinite(torch.log(A))).sum())
    return dead
print(count_dead(torch.bfloat16, False)) # 6
print(count_dead(torch.bfloat16, True))  # 0
```

**Duplicate-work check:** Prior PR #47842 addressed the same issue but is **closed, not merged** (no longer open). Verified via `gh pr list --repo huggingface/transformers --state open --search "47831 in:body"` → 0 open. This PR is a successor with the same 50+/10- dtype fix, re-applied on top of current `main` (`c7e57f7`) and ready for review. Issue #47831 author (@Nkluge-correa) invited a PR in the issue body.

## Code Agent Policy

The Transformers repo is currently being overwhelmed by a large number of PRs and issue comments written by
code agents. These often are low-quality, or fix extremely minor issues that occur rarely or never in practice.
As a result, we're instituting a rule that **first-time contributors should not use code agents to submit PRs or issues**.
We'd also ask autonomous "OpenClaw"-like agents not to open any PRs or issues.

Issues/PRs from first-time contributors that violate this rule will probably just be closed without review, and we
might block you, especially if you open more than one or appear to be deliberately ignoring this. We especially do not
want new contributors to jump in on random issues to contribute an agent-written fix. This creates lots of noise
for reviewers and other users and will almost certainly get you blocked.

For more information, please read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Before submitting

- [x] Did you read the [contributor guideline](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/contributing) and the [Pull Request](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/pr_checks) checks?

Existing `ruff`/`make style` pass; CI will run `make fix-repo` to verify `modular→modeling` copies.

## Who can review?

Anyone in the community is free to review the PR once the tests have passed. Feel free to tag members/contributors who may be interested in your PR.

title: ASR pipeline silently destroys stereo audio in channels-last layout (what soundfile/librosa return): mean(axis=0) averages across time
body:
### System Info

- transformers 5.7.0
- torch 2.11.0, numpy 1.26.4, soundfile 0.13.1
- Python 3.12, macOS, CPU

### Who can help?

`AutomaticSpeechRecognitionPipeline` / audio pipelines.

### Reproduction

Passing a stereo waveform loaded with `soundfile` silently discards almost all of the
audio. The pipeline logs a warning saying it converted to mono, and then transcribes
about 3 seconds of speech as `' you'`.

```python
import io, numpy as np, soundfile as sf
from transformers import pipeline

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
mono = (rng.standard_normal(16000 * 3) * 0.05).astype(np.float32)
buf = io.BytesIO()
sf.write(buf, np.stack([mono, mono], axis=1), 16000, format="WAV", subtype="FLOAT")
buf.seek(0)

stereo, sr = sf.read(buf, dtype="float32")     # soundfile returns (samples, channels)
print("soundfile.read shape :", stereo.shape)

asr = pipeline("automatic-speech-recognition", model="openai/whisper-tiny", device="cpu")
print("mono   :", repr(asr(mono.copy())["text"]))
print("stereo :", repr(asr(stereo.copy())["text"]))
print("after pipeline's mean(axis=0):", stereo.mean(axis=0).shape)
```

Output:

```
soundfile.read shape : (48000, 2)
UserWarning: We expect a single channel audio input for AutomaticSpeechRecognitionPipeline,
             got 2. Taking the mean of the channels for mono conversion.
mono   : ' See you in the next video!'
stereo : ' you'
after pipeline's mean(axis=0): (2,)
```

### Expected behavior

The stereo call should transcribe the same as the mono call. Instead 48,000 samples
become 2.

`pipelines/automatic_speech_recognition.py`:

```python
if inputs.ndim != 1:
    logger.warning(
        f"We expect a single channel audio input for AutomaticSpeechRecognitionPipeline, "
        f"got {inputs.ndim}. Taking the mean of the channels for mono conversion."
    )
    inputs = inputs.mean(axis=0)
```

`mean(axis=0)` assumes channels-first, `(channels, samples)`. `soundfile.read` and
`librosa.load(..., mono=False)` both return channels-last, `(samples, channels)`, which is
also what `scipy.io.wavfile.read` returns. On that layout `axis=0` averages across **time**,
so a 3-second stereo clip collapses to 2 numbers, gets padded back to 30s of silence, and
decodes to `' you'`.

`(2, N)` input works correctly, so whether the pipeline destroys your audio depends on
which loader you used, with no error either way.

Two smaller things in the same three lines:

- The warning interpolates `inputs.ndim`, not the channel count, so it always says
  "got 2" for any 2-D input regardless of how many channels there are. For the
  channels-last case the number that would actually help ("got 48000") never appears.
- A user who reads the warning is told the conversion happened. It did, along the wrong
  axis.

Suggested fix: treat the smaller of the two dimensions as the channel axis, which is
unambiguous for any realistic audio since channels are ~1-8 and samples are thousands:

```python
if inputs.ndim != 1:
    ch_axis = int(np.argmin(inputs.shape))
    logger.warning(
        f"We expect a single channel audio input for AutomaticSpeechRecognitionPipeline, "
        f"got shape {tuple(inputs.shape)}. Taking the mean over axis {ch_axis} for mono conversion."
    )
    inputs = inputs.mean(axis=ch_axis)
```

Raising on `ndim > 2` would also be reasonable. Happy to open a PR with tests covering
both layouts if you would like.

- torch 2.11.0, numpy 1.26.4
- Python 3.12, macOS, CPU

### Who can help?

Whisper / audio feature extraction.

### Reproduction

One non-finite sample anywhere in the waveform makes `WhisperFeatureExtractor` return an
input-feature matrix that is **entirely** NaN, and the ASR pipeline then produces a
confident transcription from it with no error and no warning.

```python
import numpy as np
from transformers import WhisperFeatureExtractor, pipeline

fe = WhisperFeatureExtractor.from_pretrained("openai/whisper-tiny")
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
audio = (rng.standard_normal(16000) * 0.05).astype(np.float32)
audio[8000] = np.nan                      # one non-finite sample in 16,000

feats = fe(audio, sampling_rate=16000, return_tensors="np")["input_features"]
print("input non-finite samples :", int((~np.isfinite(audio)).sum()), "/", audio.size)
print("output NaN fraction      :", float(np.isnan(feats).mean()))

asr = pipeline("automatic-speech-recognition", model="openai/whisper-tiny", device="cpu")
print("transcription            :", repr(asr(audio)["text"]))
```

Output:

```
input non-finite samples : 1 / 16000
output NaN fraction      : 1.0
transcription            : '0'
```

### Expected behavior

A single corrupt sample is 0.006% of the input and destroys 100% of the output.

The amplification happens at the dynamic-range floor in `_np_extract_fbank_features`:

```python
log_spec = np.maximum(log_spec, log_spec.max() - 8.0)
```

`log_spec.max()` is NaN if any element is NaN, and `np.maximum(x, nan)` is NaN elementwise,
so one bad sample propagates to every one of the 80 x 3000 bins. The torch path has the
same line. Without that floor the damage would stay local to the affected frames.

What makes this worth reporting is not the NaN itself but that it is silent. `generate()`
runs on all-NaN features and emits `'0'`, which is indistinguishable from a real
transcription downstream. Non-finite samples are not exotic in production audio: packet
loss, a failed resample, division by a zero-energy normalisation window, or a truncated
decode all produce them, and a caller batching thousands of files has no signal that one
of them silently returned garbage instead of failing.

Same behaviour for all-NaN and all-inf input. `float("inf")` input also yields `'0'`.

Possible fixes, in rough order of how invasive they are:

1. Validate in the feature extractor: raise `ValueError` if the waveform is not finite.
   Clearest failure, but it is a behaviour change for anyone currently relying on
   garbage-in-garbage-out.
2. Keep the damage local: compute the floor with `np.nanmax` so only the affected frames
   are NaN rather than the whole matrix. This alone still transcribes silently.
3. Warn rather than raise, on the same footing as the existing sampling-rate mismatch
   warning.

I would suggest 1, with 3 as the conservative alternative. Happy to open a PR for whichever
you prefer, including tests.

Related but separate, so I have not folded it in: a zero-length array is padded to 30s and
transcribed as `' you'` rather than rejected.
